definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of having an inflated tubular basal portion that widens gradually toward a distal limb or lobes.
other_axioms: Keep as a sibling of tubular, funnel-shaped, and cup-shaped; do not make it a subclass of every bell-bearing anatomical entity.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PATO master@83ec8697a02e3ef07beb9f5ea0256670ab1a4b15.
counterexample_or_caveat: The term is commonly applied to a corolla, but the quality itself is bearer-independent; no fixed size ratio is asserted.

definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of being long, very slender, and terete, thereby resembling a thread.
other_axioms: Sibling rather than synonym of linear; do not assert disjointness because borderline usages occur.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PATO master; PATO:0001199 linear and PATO:0104016 terete are present but not equivalent.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some glossaries use thread-like loosely; the operational definition follows the independently attested terete sense.

definition: A shape quality inhering in a flat bearer by virtue of having two approximately triangular basal lobes directed outward to either side of the main axis.
other_axioms: Sibling of PATO:0001881 arrow-shaped/sagittate; do not add hastate as its synonym and do not assert hard disjointness.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PATO master; sagittate is an exact synonym of PATO:0001881.
counterexample_or_caveat: Sagittate lobes are directed downward whereas hastate lobes are directed outward; transitional descriptions such as sagittate-hastate argue against disjointness.

other_axioms: Do not assign one exact ISCC-NBS block or prototype unless the class is explicitly scoped to a named color standard.
current_ontology_status: No atomic crimson class in pinned PATO; FLOPO contains corpus-specific crimson derivatives currently placed under red.
counterexample_or_caveat: NBS SP 440 maps crimson to several blocks across source dictionaries, so a single vivid-red or purplish-red prototype would misrepresent botanical usage.

other_axioms: Do not assign one exact vivid-red or vivid-reddish-orange block unless the class is explicitly scoped to a named color standard.
current_ontology_status: No atomic scarlet class in pinned PATO; FLOPO contains corpus-specific scarlet derivatives currently placed under red.
counterexample_or_caveat: NBS SP 440 records multiple source-dependent placements, spanning red and reddish-orange families.

definition: A plant appearance having a pale white-to-grey visual field with metallic or specular lustre; when the field usage instead denotes pale hairs, wax, or bloom, that causal phenotype is represented separately.
other_axioms: Use Saccardo category 1 as the source-qualified prototype for silver-coloured, composed from a white or pale colour component and reflectivity such as PATO:0001373 glistening; distinguish dense pale trichomes and wax or bloom rather than inferring one mechanism from the word alone.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0980092 silvery is currently a subclass of PATO:0000950 grey, but Saccardo defines silver-coloured by white plus metallic lustre and no atomic silver term exists in pinned PATO.
counterexample_or_caveat: The same field appearance can arise through different colours, reflective properties, hairs, or coatings. The historic plate may have aged, and an sRGB value would not encode metallic reflectance.

other_axioms: Disambiguate at mention level among orchid labellum, a lip of a fused bilabiate corolla, other functional lip structures, and non-anatomical topographic uses.
current_ontology_status: No general lip class in pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: A taxon-free exact mapping is unsafe because the structures called lip are not homologous and some corpus uses are geographical prose.

definition: A petal that is the specialized median member of the inner perianth whorl of a flower of Orchidaceae.
other_axioms: Record the Orchidaceae scope in the label, definition, and taxon constraint or scope note; lip is only a taxon/context-dependent synonym.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PO v2026-01-09.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not merge with staminode-derived labella in Cannaceae or with a lip made from fused portions of multiple petals.

definition: A collective organ part structure composed of distal portions of one or more fused petals that form one side of a bilabiate corolla.
other_axioms: Upper corolla lip and lower corolla lip may be subclasses; bare lip remains a related, context-dependent synonym.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PO v2026-01-09.
counterexample_or_caveat: The broader functional notion of a floral lip can be realized by structures other than fused petals, so this class must remain explicitly corolla-specific.

definition: A collective organ part structure composed of the proximal fused portions of two or more petals in a fused corolla, extending distally to where the petal portions diverge or become free.
other_axioms: Do not assert has_part some fused petal, because the tube contains portions of the petals rather than each entire petal.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PO; PO:0025581 fused corolla and PO:0025583 fused petal are present.
counterexample_or_caveat: In a gradually widening corolla the distal boundary can be conventional rather than sharply demarcated.

definition: A plant anatomical entity at the distal entrance to a corolla tube.
other_axioms: Resolve whether PO should distinguish the opening, which is a plant anatomical space, from the surrounding distal tube region, which is structural tissue.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: NYBG defines the opening, while flora phrases assigning color or markings in the throat generally target the surrounding tissue; one class cannot safely serve both without an explicit sense decision.

definition: A swollen portion of a shoot axis in an orchid that stores water or nutrients and is not a true bulb.
other_axioms: Choose between shoot axis and cardinal organ part after PO modeling review; remove or narrow the current pseudobulb synonym under corm if a distinct class is accepted.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025355 corm has pseudobulb as a NARROW synonym, but corm is defined as an entire shoot system with a short enlarged stem.
counterexample_or_caveat: Pseudobulbs may contain one or several internodes and can be above ground; treating every pseudobulb as a corm or every one as an entire shoot system overclaims.

definition: A dry, papery outer covering of a bulb or corm formed from outer leaf bases.
other_axioms: Prefer separate bulb tunic and corm tunic subclasses with the appropriate part_of target; decide whether each tunic is a leaf base/scale leaf or a collective phyllome structure.
current_ontology_status: No current live PO tunic class; PO:0006302 obsolete tunica is an unrelated meristem-layer term.
counterexample_or_caveat: Not every bulb has a tunic, so only tunic part_of bulb is safe; bulb has_part tunic is not universal. Singular tunic and plural tunics may denote a covering versus its individual layers.

definition: A plant organ of a parasitic plant that penetrates host tissue and forms a connection through which water or nutrients can be transferred between host and parasite.
other_axioms: Do not assert generic part_of root or stem; root haustorium and stem haustorium may be subclasses when developmental origin is known.
current_ontology_status: PO:0003004 haustorial root is obsolete without a replacement; no generic live haustorium class exists in pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Terminal haustoria are root-derived, but lateral haustoria can arise from root or stem tissues, including Cuscuta stem haustoria.

definition: A ring or series of floral appendages situated between the corolla and androecium and derived from petals, stamens, or both.
other_axioms: Use an origin-neutral generic class only as a parent; map a mention to corolline, staminal, or gynostegial corona when its developmental origin is supported.
current_ontology_status: No floral corona or gynostegium class in pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Attachment position does not prove developmental origin, and a generic corona must not be universally part_of either corolla or androecium.

definition: A floral corona whose appendages develop from the corolla.
other_axioms: Assert the corolla parthood only for this origin-specific subtype.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Evidence is taxon-specific; the definition is general but each annotation still requires origin evidence.

definition: A floral corona whose appendages develop from stamen filaments or a filament tube.
other_axioms: Assert androecium parthood only for this origin-specific subtype.
current_ontology_status: Absent from pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not infer staminal origin merely because a corona is adjacent or secondarily adnate to stamens.

definition: A floral corona associated developmentally and structurally with a gynostegium.
other_axioms: Define gynostegium in PO and verify the origin of the relevant corona parts before asserting parthood.
current_ontology_status: Neither gynostegium nor gynostegial corona exists in pinned PO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Gynostegial position alone does not determine whether every component is corolline or androecial.

definition: A whole-plant phenotype in which, after some growth, the plant cannot mechanically sustain its stem without an external support.
other_axioms: Retain as a primitive evidence-defined phenotype until a suitable relation to an external support is selected; make liana and vine narrower phenotypes.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900035 whole plant lianescent currently has climber and liana as exact synonyms but no definition or logical characterization.
counterexample_or_caveat: Climbing is support dependence, not merely a coiled, flexible, long, or prostrate stem; those qualities alone are insufficient.

definition: A whole-plant climbing phenotype in which the climbing axes are woody throughout their length.
other_axioms: Combine the support-dependent climber phenotype with PATO:0002348 ligneous on the relevant shoot axes.
current_ontology_status: Liana is currently an exact synonym of FLOPO:0900035, conflated with the broader climber sense.
counterexample_or_caveat: The historical word can be used more broadly, but the cited standardization recommends the woody restriction.

definition: A whole-plant climbing phenotype in which the climbing axes are herbaceous or otherwise non-woody.
other_axioms: Combine the support-dependent climber phenotype with PATO:0002352 herbaceous on the relevant shoot axes.
current_ontology_status: PO:0000003 carries vine only as a NARROW synonym; FLOPO lacks a distinct defined vine phenotype.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some English usage calls woody climbers vines; the proposed class follows the cited standardized technical sense.

definition: A climbing phenotype in which the plant grows over support without active searching movement or a specialized attachment structure.
other_axioms: Represent as a narrower climbing mechanism; avoid inventing a PATO shape that equates absence of a specialized attachment organ with a bearer-intrinsic form.
current_ontology_status: No corresponding PO/PATO/FLOPO class in the pinned artifacts.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some scramblers possess hooks or spines; the source distinguishes simple scrambling from hook-assisted passive climbing, so context may require a narrower mechanism.

definition: A climbing phenotype in which the main stem coils helically around an external support.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0000404 coiled for stem shape only as one component; retain the relation to an external support so a free coil is not classified as twining.
current_ontology_status: No corresponding defined FLOPO class; PATO:0000404 coiled is necessary but not sufficient.
counterexample_or_caveat: Twining petioles, tendrils, and inflorescences are different mechanisms and must not be normalized to main-stem twining.

definition: A botanical color phenotype whose description records two or more color components without asserting that the phenotype is a subclass of each component color.
other_axioms: Use FLOPO has_quality_component restrictions to the PATO components; do not create every compound in PATO and do not use multiple PATO is_a parents.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO already defines a has_quality_component property and uses it for imported compound values.
counterexample_or_caveat: A mixture, transition, spotting pattern, and region-qualified combination are not interchangeable; preserve the construction and location from the source phrase.

surface_forms: greenish or pinkish|color or color|colour or colour
definition: A botanical color phenotype for which the source leaves two or more color values as alternatives.
other_axioms: Define the class with owl:unionOf the alternatives; never encode an or phrase as conjunctive parents or as multiple component restrictions.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0980199 greenish or pinkish and other imported alternatives already use owl:unionOf in ontology/flopo.owl.
counterexample_or_caveat: A union preserves uncertainty in the source; it does not mean one specimen simultaneously bears every alternative.

definition: A whole-plant phenotype in which the plant lacks all leaves at the described life stage.
other_axioms: Compose PO:0000003 whole plant with PATO:0002000 lacks all parts of type toward PO:0025034 leaf, while retaining life-stage context.
current_ontology_status: No dedicated defined FLOPO class identified; the required PO/PATO components exist.
counterexample_or_caveat: Deciduous plants can be leafless temporarily, and reduced scales may or may not count as leaves for a particular description; do not infer a permanent taxon property.

definition: A whole-plant phenotype in which leaves are sufficiently numerous or conspicuous to dominate the described shoot appearance.
other_axioms: Do not reduce leafy to has_part some leaf. Select a comparative amount, density, or coverage model only after corpus examples establish the intended baseline.
current_ontology_status: No dedicated defined FLOPO class identified; PATO cardinality and amount qualities exist but none is yet proven exact.
counterexample_or_caveat: Almost every normal vascular plant has at least one leaf, so simple presence would make the phenotype uninformative and wrong.

definition: A whole-plant phenotype characterized by dense branching and a compact, spreading shoot architecture.
other_axioms: Likely compose branchiness, branch density, and branch position; do not map automatically to shrub because herbs and other non-woody plants can be bushy.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900034 whole plant frutescent has bush and shrub as exact synonyms, but bushy is not equivalent to being a shrub.
counterexample_or_caveat: A bushy herb is not a shrub; an evidence-backed operational threshold or comparative reference is still needed.

definition: A phenotype in which the described plant structure has branches.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0000402 branched on the actual bearer recovered from context; create a whole-plant convenience class only if corpus normalization requires it.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000402 branched exists; the missing normalization is chiefly bearer/context resolution rather than an ontology gap.
counterexample_or_caveat: Branching can describe a stem, inflorescence, root, or whole-plant habit, so one context-free FLOPO target would conflate bearers.

surface_forms: male flower|male flowers|female flower|female flowers|staminate flower|staminate flowers|pistillate flower|pistillate flowers
other_axioms: Map staminate/male flower senses to PO:0025600 and pistillate/female flower senses to PO:0025599 after corpus-sense review; consider promoting the current RELATED male/female synonyms only through a PO proposal.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025599 pistillate flower and PO:0025600 staminate flower are current defined classes; male flower and female flower are RELATED synonyms.
counterexample_or_caveat: Male/female may describe the plant, reproductive function, or a flower with aborted organs; do not compose generic PATO sex qualities without checking that the PO definitions match.

other_axioms: Map a focal plant growth-form mention to FLOPO:0900034; retain PO:0000003 only as a broader anatomical target when an entity rather than a phenotype is required.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900034 has shrub and bush as exact synonyms; PO:0000003 has both only as NARROW synonyms.
counterexample_or_caveat: Many bush occurrences describe a support or habitat plant rather than the focal taxon, so extraction must bind the mention before asserting a phenotype.

other_axioms: Map focal growth-form uses to FLOPO:0900033; retain PO:0000003 only as the broader entity target when appropriate.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900033 has tree as an exact synonym; PO:0000003 has tree only as a NARROW synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: The word also occurs in comparisons and habitat prose; normalization does not by itself establish that the focal taxon is a tree.

other_axioms: Use FLOPO:0900039 when woody describes the focal shoot axis; PATO:0002348 ligneous is the underlying quality but does not currently carry woody as an exact synonym.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900039 has woody as an exact synonym but lacks a textual definition and explicit EQ characterization.
counterexample_or_caveat: Corpus uses include woody herb, woody shrub, and woody fruit/stem contexts; verify the bearer rather than attaching the shoot-axis phenotype blindly.

other_axioms: Map the anatomical entity to PO:0025615; construct a FLOPO assertion only after binding its qualities or relation to the focal plant.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025615 is a defined collective leaf structure; its exact preferred label is rosette.
counterexample_or_caveat: Most corpus uses are basal leaf rosettes, but OCR and comparative prose still require mention-level verification.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030117 for the anatomical inflorescence and FLOPO:0900001 when the desired output is the corresponding inflorescence-type phenotype.
current_ontology_status: Both PO:0030117 spike inflorescence and FLOPO:0900001 inflorescence type spike are exact lexical candidates.
counterexample_or_caveat: Spike can also occur in non-inflorescence compounds and OCR fragments; the PO/FLOPO collision is a representation choice, not evidence that both should be asserted automatically.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030121 or FLOPO:0900005 only for the flower-head/capitulum sense; reject topographic head of wadi, road, or descent uses.
current_ontology_status: PO:0030121 has head as a BROAD synonym; FLOPO:0900005 has head as an exact synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: The corpus contains several topographic occurrences and generic rounded heads that may not satisfy the capitulum definition.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030091 for the fruit entity and FLOPO:0900012 for the corresponding fruit-type phenotype.
current_ontology_status: Both PO:0030091 capsule fruit and FLOPO:0900012 fruit type capsule are exact lexical candidates.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not confuse a botanical capsule fruit with non-botanical capsule senses; extraction must also distinguish entity mention from phenotype assertion.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030108 for the fruit entity and FLOPO:0900015 for the corresponding fruit-type phenotype.
current_ontology_status: Both PO:0030108 berry fruit and FLOPO:0900015 fruit type berry are exact lexical candidates.
counterexample_or_caveat: A fruit called berry in vernacular prose may not meet the botanical definition; retain context and do not infer type from unrelated comparisons.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030126 for the anatomical entity and FLOPO:0900006 for the corresponding inflorescence-type phenotype.
current_ontology_status: Both PO:0030126 cyme inflorescence and FLOPO:0900006 inflorescence type cyme are exact lexical candidates.
counterexample_or_caveat: The corpus includes comparative statements about cyme shapes; the extractor must identify the focal bearer and assertion.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030121 for the entity and FLOPO:0900005 for its phenotype representation.
current_ontology_status: PO:0030121 and FLOPO:0900005 are both exact candidates after removing PO's editorial synonym-scope suffix.
counterexample_or_caveat: The frozen occurrence is explanatory prose comparing a capitulum with a flower, not necessarily a phenotype assertion about the focal taxon.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030129 for the anatomical entity and FLOPO:0900003 for the corresponding inflorescence-type phenotype.
current_ontology_status: Both PO:0030129 umbel inflorescence and FLOPO:0900003 inflorescence type umbel are exact lexical candidates.
counterexample_or_caveat: The source context must still distinguish the entity from the phenotype class and from umbel-like arrangements.

other_axioms: Use PO:0030100 legume fruit or PO:0030105 follicle fruit only when morphology/taxon resolves the broad word pod; use FLOPO:0900013 only for the legume-phenotype sense.
current_ontology_status: PO treats pod as NARROW for both legume fruit and follicle fruit; FLOPO:0900013 has pod as an exact synonym of fruit type legume.
counterexample_or_caveat: Pod is not universally equivalent to legume fruit, so FLOPO's current exact synonym is too strong for unqualified normalization.

other_axioms: Map the shape quality to PATO:0005005 after binding the bearer.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0005005 is a current defined exact-label match.
counterexample_or_caveat: The corpus predominantly describes stems expanding from a center; radiating energy or process senses would require rejection.

other_axioms: Map the edge-shape quality to PATO:0040008 after binding the bearer.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0040008 is a current defined exact-label match.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some botanical fringes are hairs or appendages rather than textile-like threads; the current PATO definition should be checked for adequate biological breadth.

other_axioms: Map the shape quality to PATO:0005002 after binding the bearer.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0005002 is a current defined exact-label match.
counterexample_or_caveat: One OCR-fragment context is incomplete; mapping the term does not validate the surrounding extraction.

definition: A whole-plant phenotype in which the plant is non-woody, usually with soft stems.
other_axioms: Add herb as an exact synonym of FLOPO:0022142 whole plant herbaceous rather than leaving only the non-discriminating broad mapping to PO:0000003.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0022142 already defines whole plant has-quality some PATO:0002352 herbaceous; PO:0000003 has herb only as a NARROW synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: Herb can occur in habitat or comparison prose, and some subshrubs are described informally as herbs; extraction still requires focal-taxon binding.

definition: A text construction in which wide links a numeric quantity and unit to the width attribute of a bearer.
other_axioms: When preceded by a numeric quantity, normalize to PATO:0000921 width plus the parsed value and unit, not to PATO:0000600 increased width; retain a separate closeMatch candidate for genuinely comparative wide.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000600 carries wide only as a RELATED synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: At least 1051 of 1201 raw whole-word occurrences (87.5%) match a conservative number-plus-unit pattern; treating these as increased width would discard the measurement and assert a comparison absent from the text.

definition: A text construction in which tall or high links a numeric quantity and unit to the height attribute of a bearer.
other_axioms: When preceded by a numeric quantity, normalize to PATO:0000119 height plus the parsed value and unit, not to PATO:0000570 increased height; use context to reject altitude and non-focal uses.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000570 carries tall only as a RELATED synonym; high has no safe single lexical target in the current report.
counterexample_or_caveat: The conservative number-plus-unit pattern covers 322 of 333 raw tall occurrences (96.7%) and 533 of 553 high occurrences (96.4%); high also frequently denotes altitude.

other_axioms: Propose reviewed skos:closeMatch mappings while preserving PATO's RELATED synonym scope; bind the adjective to the focal botanical bearer before using it.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000587 has small and tiny as RELATED synonyms.
counterexample_or_caveat: Small and tiny are context-dependent comparisons and also modify habitats or groups; do not convert them to absolute size ranges or accept every mention as a focal phenotype.

other_axioms: Propose a reviewed skos:closeMatch while preserving PATO's RELATED synonym scope; use PATO:0000921 width with a number when an explicit measurement is supplied.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000599 has narrow as a RELATED synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: Narrow is relative to a comparison class and also modifies ravines and other habitat entities, so bearer binding is mandatory.

other_axioms: Propose a reviewed skos:closeMatch while preserving PATO's RELATED synonym scope and requiring focal-bearer binding.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000586 has large as a RELATED synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: Corpus uses include large groves, gullies, and other habitat objects; a lexical match alone is not a taxon phenotype.

other_axioms: Propose a reviewed skos:closeMatch while preserving PATO's RELATED synonym scope; route explicit numeric thickness to the thickness attribute and value instead.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000591 has thick as a RELATED synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: Thick may describe roots, leaves, stems, hair tufts, or a numeric measurement, so the bearer and construction must be retained.

other_axioms: Propose a reviewed skos:closeMatch while preserving PATO's RELATED synonym scope; route explicit numeric thickness to the thickness attribute and value instead.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000592 has thin as a RELATED synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: Thin can express thickness, width, sparseness, or consistency; context must establish the intended attribute.

definition: A pilosity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being covered with short hairs or soft down.
other_axioms: Use and revise PATO:0001320; add botanical pubescent/pubescence and downy as synonyms, and never map the botanical sense to PATO:0000455. Prepare a FLOPO signature migration from PATO:0000455 to PATO:0001320 for all affected pubescent phenotypes.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001320 already has essentially this definition and is a child of hairy; PATO:0000455 is a maturity quality meaning onset of sexual puberty.
counterexample_or_caveat: Downy emphasizes especially short, weak, soft hairs and may merit a narrower subclass if curators require that distinction; the migration itself is unambiguous because all affected FLOPO bearers are plant structures.

other_axioms: Exclude these surface hits from phenotype normalization when their concordance is a substrate, geological feature, illumination environment, or locality phrase; retain the text for ecological or provenance extraction.
current_ontology_status: These misses are not evidence of missing PO, PATO, or FLOPO classes for the phenotype task.
counterexample_or_caveat: The same words can have anatomical or quality senses in another corpus, so rejection must be construction- and context-specific rather than a global stop-word rule.

other_axioms: Exclude current uses such as locally abundant, nowhere abundant, and abundant in a region from individual-plant phenotype extraction; retain them for population or occurrence modeling.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi uses express population abundance or geographic occurrence rather than a quality of a focal plant structure.
counterexample_or_caveat: Abundant hairs, flowers, or other bearer-bound parts could express a phenotype in future text and must not be rejected by token alone.

definition: A text construction in which a botanical head or suffix combines with one or more preceding modifiers to describe the entity, number, shape, colour, or other quality of a bearer.
other_axioms: Parse the complete compound, including hyphen-separated and OCR-separated forms, then normalize its head and modifiers compositionally; do not coin a class or value for the isolated suffix fragment.
current_ontology_status: The current misses are chiefly fragments of forms such as weak-stemmed, fleshy-leaved, two-seeded, mango-shaped, red-edged, and long-tubed.
counterexample_or_caveat: Foliolate and similar adjectives can be legitimate full terms in other constructions; preserve the exact source span and only apply this treatment when the larger compound is recoverable.

definition: A text construction in which an adverb modifies the degree, density, manner, or transition of an explicitly stated botanical quality.
other_axioms: Attach the modifier to the quality in the same syntactic construction, for example sparsely branched or strongly reflexed; do not normalize the adverb as a standalone phenotype value.
current_ontology_status: The current registry treats these modifiers as isolated missing surfaces even though their semantics depend on the modified quality.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some modifiers require different models: sparsely may change density, abruptly may describe a transition, and barely may fall below an assertion threshold; one generic PATO class would conflate them.

definition: A plant structure that is a whole organism.
other_axioms: Add plant as an exact English synonym and plants as its exact plural synonym on PO:0000003, then require focal-taxon or bearer binding during extraction.
current_ontology_status: PO:0000003 is the defined whole-organism class but lacks the ordinary English singular and plural words plant and plants.
counterexample_or_caveat: The Saudi text also uses plant in taxonomic, comparative, and discourse statements; a lexical match identifies an entity mention but does not itself assert a phenotype.

other_axioms: Normalize constructions such as flowers in clusters or clustered flowers to PATO:0001629 only after binding the repeated bearer; preserve an anatomical collective entity when the text names one instead.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001629 is defined as an irregular spatial pattern and has clustered as an exact synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: A cluster noun can denote an entity or inflorescence rather than a spatial quality, and among clusters of bracts does not license attaching aggregated to every nearby bearer.

other_axioms: Use PO:0025005 only when context identifies a laminar plant organ, and prefer an existing bearer-specific descendant such as leaf lamina margin when the bearer is known.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025005 is a defined cardinal organ part, part of a plant organ lamina; the missing normalization is mainly bearer resolution and ordinary-word synonymy.
counterexample_or_caveat: Margin may denote a leaf, petal, lobe, geographical edge, or page boundary, so the unqualified token is not a context-free exact mapping.

definition: A plant structure that is the distal portion of another plant structure.
other_axioms: Use as a generic parent for compatible existing organ, axis, and trichome apex classes; add apices as the exact plural and retain PO's distinction between an extended apex region and its apical-most tip.
current_ontology_status: PO contains many bearer-specific apex classes but no generic plant structure apex that can normalize an unqualified, context-bound apex mention.
counterexample_or_caveat: Distal depends on the bearer's axis, and the NYBG glossary uses tip more broadly than PO; do not make all existing tip classes exact synonyms of apex.

definition: A plant structure that is the proximal portion of another plant structure.
other_axioms: Use as a generic parent for compatible existing base classes while retaining bearer-specific subclasses such as leaf base and stem base.
current_ontology_status: PO contains multiple bearer-specific base classes but no generic plant structure base for a context-bound unqualified mention.
counterexample_or_caveat: Proximal orientation must be established from the bearer; base can also denote a support, attachment site, chemical base, locality, or numerical radix outside this botanical construction.

definition: A cardinal organ part that is a projection arising from the margin or base of a plant organ lamina.
other_axioms: Introduce only after reconciling the generic boundary, then place PO:0025514 phyllome lamina lobe beneath it and resolve corolla- and petal-lobe mentions through their actual bearer.
current_ontology_status: PO has phyllome and leaf lamina lobe classes but no generic lamina-lobe parent; PO:0025514 uses a one-quarter-or-more sinus threshold.
counterexample_or_caveat: NYBG specifies rounded projections and elsewhere a less-than-half cut for lobed leaf margins, while PO allows rounded or angular lobes and uses a different depth threshold; the generic definition must not silently erase that disagreement.

definition: A hair-like outgrowth of the plant epidermis.
other_axioms: Do not mint a hair subclass without a distinguishing characteristic. Review changing botanical hair from a NARROW synonym of PO:0000282 to an exact or related synonym, and add the plural with OMO:0003004.
current_ontology_status: PO:0000282 already defines trichome and carries hair as a NARROW synonym, but the botanical glossaries redirect hair to trichome rather than defining a narrower anatomical kind.
counterexample_or_caveat: Both singular Saudi occurrences are the place name Hair, whereas plural hairs is anatomical; extraction must retain case and bearer context even if PO revises the synonym scope.

definition: A stem that is the main stem of a tree.
other_axioms: Promote the current NARROW synonym on stem to an exact synonym of this subclass; keep bole as a candidate synonym subject to the narrower unbranched-portion convention.
current_ontology_status: PO:0009047 has trunk only as a NARROW synonym and no defined trunk subclass.
counterexample_or_caveat: One source equates trunk with an unbranched bole, while another includes buttresses and prop roots; the proposed class conservatively includes only the main stem and does not misclassify roots as stem parts.

definition: A vascular leaf of a fern, cycad, or palm, including its lamina and stipe or petiole when present.
other_axioms: Promote the current NARROW synonym on vascular leaf to the exact label of this subclass; do not assert a universal whole-plant, stipe, or petiole restriction because a frond may be detached and a stipe or petiole may be absent or reduced.
current_ontology_status: PO:0009025 carries frond as a NARROW synonym but lacks a defined subclass; 11 of 12 Saudi mentions describe palm leaves.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some botanists restrict frond to ferns, while broader authoritative glossaries include palms and cycads; the lone Saudi singular occurrence is frond-like and must remain a resemblance rather than an entity assertion.

definition: A cardinal organ part that is a primary division of a pinnately compound leaf.
other_axioms: Promote the current NARROW synonym on leaflet to this class, with pinnae as the exact plural; do not assert pinna SubClassOf leaflet because a primary pinna need not be an ultimate segment in a multiply divided leaf.
current_ontology_status: PO:0020049 leaflet carries pinna and pinnae as NARROW synonyms even though leaflet is defined as an ultimate compound-leaf segment.
counterexample_or_caveat: In a once-pinnate leaf a pinna can also satisfy leaflet, but that overlap does not hold for a bipinnate or more-divided leaf.

definition: A cardinal organ part that is a secondary or higher-order division of a pinnately compound leaf.
other_axioms: Promote the current NARROW synonym on leaflet to this class; retain the transitive part-of relation to the compound leaf and add an exact plural synonym.
current_ontology_status: PO:0020049 carries pinnule as a NARROW synonym but an intermediate pinnule is not necessarily the ultimate segment required by the leaflet definition.
counterexample_or_caveat: Higher-order terminology varies among fern treatments, and the source's worked-example sentence is corrupt; only the clear secondary-or-higher division is used.

definition: An inflorescence consisting of several naked staminate flowers, usually one naked pistillate flower, and a subtending cup-shaped involucre.
other_axioms: Remove cyathium and cyathia as NARROW synonyms of PO:0030126 cyme inflorescence; add them as exact singular and plural labels here; assert has_part some PO:0025600 and has_part some PO:0009100, but not a universal pistillate-flower or whole-plant parthood restriction.
current_ontology_status: PO currently puts cyathium under cyme only as a NARROW synonym, but the cyme definition requires paired determinate higher-order axes and pedicellate flowers and does not define a cyathium.
counterexample_or_caveat: The pistillate flower is only usual, not universal; sexed-flower and involucre axioms should use existing PO classes without treating every nearby bract as part of the cyathium.

other_axioms: Use PATO:0001370 viscid when a bearer has a sticky liquid coating and PATO:0002331 adhesive when the bearer itself, such as gum, exhibits contact adhesion; do not add one unrestricted exact synonym to both.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001370 is a coating quality that is sticky or clammy, while PATO:0002331 is the value of molecular adhesivity; NYBG equates viscid with sticky and UPOV distinguishes it from resinous.
counterexample_or_caveat: Sticky gum, stems, foliage, and whole herbs occur. The surface word alone does not determine whether a coating or the material itself realizes the adhesion, nor whether glands or resin cause it.

other_axioms: Add arching as an exact morphological variant of PATO:0001594 when the bearer forms or resembles an arch.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001594 already defines arched as forming or resembling an arch; the Saudi mentions describe arching stems and branches.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not use arched for any merely curved stem: the recognizable arch form is the differentia, and growth direction remains a separate quality when asserted.

other_axioms: Add sessile as an exact synonym of the botanical sense and retain the distinct zoological homonym.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001436 is defined as attachment without a stalk; both UPOV and the Saudi flower examples use that sense.
counterexample_or_caveat: The current PATO wording begins with a flower bearer but mentions leaves; curators may wish to make the genus definition bearer-independent before adding the plain synonym.

other_axioms: Add scented as an exact synonym of PATO:0001331 for unmodified odor-presence assertions; model sweetly, faintly, or strongly scented compositionally.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001331 denotes having odor, whereas PATO:0002191 aromatic is an unrelated molecular aromaticity class.
counterexample_or_caveat: Scented does not say whether the odor is pleasant, strong, or chemically aromatic; those modifiers require distinct evidence and must not be inferred.

other_axioms: Use a non-exact mapping to mature for fruit contexts unless PATO accepts a narrower ripe subclass; retain PO developmental-stage mappings where the text supports a specific stage.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001701 denotes complete growth, differentiation, or development; PO contains several fruit-ripening stages but no generic exact entity target for ripe.
counterexample_or_caveat: Ripe is fruit- and use-context sensitive and is narrower than mature; green ripe fruit, edible ripeness, seed-dispersal maturity, and dry grain stages need not coincide.

definition: A shape and orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being abruptly bent backward or abaxially downward.
other_axioms: Keep distinct from PATO:0002211 recurved, which is smoothly curved backward or inward; record deflexed as an exact synonym only if PATO curators accept UPOV usage.
current_ontology_status: No reflexed class or synonym occurs in pinned PATO; bent and recurved are present but neither captures the abrupt directional differentia.
counterexample_or_caveat: UPOV also uses reflexed for an angle greater than 180 degrees; the proposed wording covers the shared abrupt-backward form without asserting a numeric angle for every bearer.

definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having one or more conspicuous, thin, flattened extensions that project from its main body.
other_axioms: Add alate as an exact synonym; do not place the class under ridged because botanical wings include both ridge-like and broader laminar extensions, and keep anatomical wing entities such as wing petals separate from this bearer-independent quality.
current_ontology_status: PATO has ridged but no winged/alate shape; PO has bearer-specific structures such as a petiole lamina and wing petal.
counterexample_or_caveat: Context must distinguish a winged bearer from an anatomical structure named a wing; the broad physical definition deliberately covers both narrow ridge-like and broader laminar botanical wings.

definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being directed gradually upward at an oblique angle.
other_axioms: Place under orientation, and compare with the established erect, decumbent, procumbent, and prostrate vocabulary without asserting a total ordering among those classes.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has erect, prostrate, decumbent, and procumbent but no ascending value; UPOV routes ascending to its gradually-upward definition.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some sources restrict ascending to an initially horizontal or spreading base; UPOV does not, so that narrower differentia is not asserted universally.

definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being directed outward and diverging from a principal axis.
other_axioms: Compare PATO:0005005 radiating, whose definition requires expansion from a center point; spreading need not be radial or prostrate. Model a whole-plant spreading growth form in FLOPO through the outward orientation of its branches or shoots rather than asserting this atomic orientation directly on the whole plant.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has no spreading value; UPOV explicitly applies spreading both to divergent branches and to whole-plant growth habit.
counterexample_or_caveat: The same word denotes an organ orientation and a whole-plant architecture; only the former is the atomic PATO quality, while FLOPO must compose the latter over the relevant parts.

definition: A pilosity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being covered with long, somewhat matted and tangled trichomes that give a wool-like appearance.
other_axioms: Add woolly only as a related synonym and distinguish PATO:0002341 tomentose, whose hairs are shorter, denser, and more matted.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO contains hairy, pubescent hair, arachnose, and tomentose but no lanate or woolly class.
counterexample_or_caveat: Woolly can also describe a non-hair material by resemblance; accept the mapping only when plant hairs, trichomes, or pubescence are the bearer-realizing structures.

definition: A pilosity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being covered with long, soft, slender, appressed trichomes that give a silk-like appearance.
other_axioms: Add silky only as a related synonym because it also denotes non-trichome texture and gloss.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has no sericeous or botanical silky pilosity class.
counterexample_or_caveat: Silky may describe texture, gloss, or a non-trichome surface outside botanical indumentum; context must establish the hair-covering sense.

definition: A plant-organ margin shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the margin being undivided and lacking teeth or lobes.
other_axioms: Use only for a plant-organ margin; the unrestricted adjective entire remains ordinary-language quantification and is not a synonym of this class in every context.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has dentate, serrate, and crenate terms but no entire-margin counterpart.
counterexample_or_caveat: Several Saudi occurrences mean the whole or complete plant rather than an untoothed margin; an exact lexical mapping without bearer/context gating would be wrong.

definition: A leaf phenotype in which the bearer is a compound leaf with exactly three leaflets.
other_axioms: Revise FLOPO:0900067 in place: remove its leaf-shape parent, place it under leaf phenotype and the proposed composition/cardinality facet, assert has_part exactly 3 PO:0020049, and associate it with a FLOPO-local trifoliolate quality under PATO:0001555. Add trifoliate only as a related synonym if curators confirm that usage.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900067 leaf trifoliolate already exists but is asserted under FLOPO:0000149 leaf shape and has neither a definition nor a logical characterization. PO supplies compound leaf and leaflet; the phenotype and its supporting quality belong in FLOPO rather than multiplying PO leaf entities.
counterexample_or_caveat: The exact cardinality concerns ultimate leaflets: a leaf with three primary pinnae that are themselves divided need not have exactly three ultimate leaflets. Correcting the parent and definition preserves the intended referent, so this is an in-place repair rather than obsoletion.

definition: A life span quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's expected natural life span being no more than one year.
other_axioms: Use annual as an exact synonym in botanical life-history context; represent the one-year boundary explicitly rather than as merely decreased life span.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has the life span attribute but no annual, biennial, or perennial values.
counterexample_or_caveat: The definition concerns expected natural life span, not the bearer's current age; plural annuals denotes plants bearing this quality and must be composed with the whole-plant entity during extraction.

definition: A life span quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's expected natural life span being at least three years.
other_axioms: Represent the three-year lower boundary explicitly and contrast annual and biennial life histories.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has the life span attribute but no perennial value.
counterexample_or_caveat: The definition concerns expected natural life span, not current age or successful seed production; the latter is not universal for sterile or vegetatively reproducing perennial plants.

definition: A whole-plant growth phenotype in which shoots arise in dense clumps or tufts from a compact base.
other_axioms: Model the whole plant as having multiple spatially aggregated shoot axes; do not map hair tufts or a noun tuft to this growth-form class.
current_ontology_status: No atomic caespitose quality exists in pinned PATO and no equivalent whole-plant class exists in released FLOPO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Tufted is polysemous: it can describe trichomes, appendage clusters, or plants growing in tussocks; the Saudi adjective predominantly denotes the whole-plant habit, while noun tufts need separate bearer analysis.

definition: A contextual phenotype pattern in which exactly one instance of a specified botanical structure occurs at the relevant bearer or site rather than in a cluster.
other_axioms: Bind the counted PO entity and bearer, then represent exact cardinality one; do not coin a PATO value or a FLOPO class for every bearer-cardinality combination.
current_ontology_status: PO defines inflorescence as having two or more flowers, so the glossary's solitary-flower wording cannot be promoted as an inflorescence subclass under current PO semantics.
counterexample_or_caveat: Single also modifies locality, stem, specimen, and discourse expressions; only bearer-bound botanical cardinality constructions instantiate this pattern.

definition: A phenotype in which veins of a plant structure are visibly distinguished from surrounding tissue by a stated colour or contrast.
other_axioms: Bind the bearer and its PO vein or vascular structure, and attach the explicitly stated colour to that structure; preserve generic prominent venation separately when no colour is stated.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi uses include red-veined sepals, silvery-veined leaves, coloured petals, palmately veined leaves, and prominent uncoloured venation; no single atomic PATO quality captures all senses.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not infer a colour when only venation topology is asserted, and do not attach the nearby colour to the whole leaf or flower when it specifically modifies the veins.

definition: A botanical odor description in which a scent is characterized as sweet by resemblance to familiar sweet-smelling prototypes rather than by a sugar taste assertion.
other_axioms: Map the scent-presence component to PATO:0001331 odorous, retain sweet as an unresolved odor-character modifier, and preserve independent faint/strong intensity modifiers.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrences overwhelmingly occur in sweet scent or sweetly scented constructions; pinned PATO has odorous but no supported sweet-odor value.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not map to a sweet taste or generic flavor class, and do not infer pleasantness: several descriptions combine sweetish character with a bad or rotting smell.

definition: A phenotype in which a plant liquid or exudate has an opaque, pale appearance resembling milk.
other_axioms: Compose the context-bound plant substance with PATO:0000963 opaque and an explicitly supported white or pale colour; leave a possible latex entity unresolved rather than inferring chemical identity from appearance.
current_ontology_status: Nearly all Saudi uses modify juice or sap; PO:0025161 covers portions of plant substance and explicitly mentions latex in its comment but PO has no generic latex class.
counterexample_or_caveat: Milky can denote appearance without establishing that the substance is latex, contains milk-like compounds, or has a particular viscosity; those claims need independent evidence.

definition: A phenotype in which a plant or plant structure bears pointed defensive projections such as prickles, thorns, or spines.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0001365 spiny as the broad surface-feature quality; when morphology is known, retain PO:0025169 prickle, PO:0025172 thorn, or the applicable spine entity rather than collapsing them.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001365 explicitly includes spines, thorns, and similar projections; PO distinguishes a superficial epidermal prickle from a branch-derived thorn.
counterexample_or_caveat: Prickly and thorny are narrower than PATO spiny and flora prose may use them loosely; exact PO organ identity cannot be inferred from the adjective alone.

other_axioms: Use PATO:0000569 only for relative height and PATO:0000587 only for relative overall size; route numeric low-height constructions through the measurement parser and reject habitat/locality uses.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO already contains decreased height and decreased size; most Saudi occurrences describe low hills, valleys, or elevations, while a minority describe low-growing plants.
counterexample_or_caveat: Low is a relational or scalar comparison whose attribute and reference population must come from context; it is not an unrestricted exact synonym of either target.

definition: A contextual phenotype that relates a plant developmental process or stage to an explicitly stated season or time interval.
other_axioms: Bind flowering or fruiting to the applicable PO plant structure development stage and model summer or winter as temporal context; do not mint atomic qualities for the isolated words.
current_ontology_status: The corpus uses night-, summer-, and winter-flowering and fruiting expressions; PO supplies development stages, while the season is contextual information rather than a plant quality.
counterexample_or_caveat: The same season word can describe collection time or habitat climate, and flowering can be a process mention rather than a phenotype value.

other_axioms: Reject taxonomic rank, editorial comparison, and discourse uses; re-run phrase-level extraction before rejection so constructions such as new shoots or new growth retain their actual developmental meaning.
current_ontology_status: These isolated spans predominantly arise from taxonomic or descriptive prose rather than phenotype values.
counterexample_or_caveat: This is a context-specific rejection, not a global stop list: form can denote morphology and new can modify a genuine plant structure or developmental stage.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure occupies a relative position along, within, or around an explicitly identified bearer or axis.
other_axioms: Bind the located PO entity, reference bearer, and axis before selecting PATO:0002349 basal to, PATO:0001195 proximal to, PATO:0001234 distal to, an axil relation, or another directionally correct relation; do not equate basal with proximal or apical with distal without that frame.
current_ontology_status: PATO has relational position vocabulary, and PO has axil and axillary-structure classes, but each adjective omits the reference entity and coordinate frame needed for a complete assertion.
counterexample_or_caveat: Lower and upper may express vertical position, serial rank, surface, or comparison; outer and inner likewise require a container or radial frame, while axillary requires the relevant axil.

definition: A phenotype that constrains the number of instances of a specified plant structure at an explicitly identified bearer or site.
other_axioms: Represent the counted PO entity and bearer, retaining few, several, or numerous as source-language cardinality bands until a glossary or dataset supplies numeric boundaries; model none as qualified absence rather than the number zero detached from a bearer.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001997 decreased amount and PATO:0000470 increased amount are comparative qualities but do not define the botanical count ranges expressed here.
counterexample_or_caveat: The words have no universal numeric boundary and do not identify what is being counted; mapping few directly to decreased amount would silently add a comparison class.

definition: A whole-plant growth phenotype in which the bearer is woody, perennial, and has multiple branches arising at or near its base.
other_axioms: Provide an evidence-backed definition for the existing whole plant frutescent/shrub class; map shrubby only when it asserts that growth form, and retain resemblance constructions such as shrubby herb for contextual composition.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900034 has exact synonyms bush and shrub but no textual definition; Saudi occurrences often modify tree or herb and therefore do not all denote literal membership in the shrub growth form.
counterexample_or_caveat: A shrubby tree can have a low-branched habit without being a shrub, and a shrubby herb may merely resemble one; an unrestricted exact mapping would overclassify both.

other_axioms: Use PATO:0000333 when a bearer has round areas of differing hue or saturation; reject locality constructions such as beauty spot and keep anatomical spots lacking colour evidence separate.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000333 already defines the coloured round-marking sense.
counterexample_or_caveat: Most plural occurrences are genuine colour markings, but singular spot includes locality prose and a spot need not be round or chromatically distinct in every domain.

other_axioms: Map corpus colour-marking occurrences to PATO:0000329 and add blotch/blotches only as lexical retrieval forms, not exact synonyms of a quality noun.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000329 defines irregularly shaped spots or blots of a different hue or saturation and already has blotched as an exact synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: A noun names a marking while PATO:0000329 denotes the bearer's pattern; extraction must preserve that bearer shift.

definition: A colour pattern inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having one or more elongated markings that differ in hue, lightness, or saturation from adjacent areas.
other_axioms: Create the orientation-neutral pattern only after a colour-pattern source is added; make PATO:0001946 banded its transverse-stripe subtype and remove the current unsafe exact synonym striped from banded.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001946 defines only transverse stripes but treats striped as exact; PlantNET defines lineolate as fine or obscure lines without requiring colour.
counterexample_or_caveat: Line, lined, and streaked can denote grooves, veins, ranks, margins, or text rather than colour. The proposed definition is not yet evidence-complete and must remain unaccepted.

other_axioms: Use PATO:0001608 for a bearer diversified with patches; reject habitat/population patches and retain coloured-patch entity mentions until bearer and colour are bound.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001608 already defines a spatial pattern marked by or consisting of patches.
counterexample_or_caveat: Patch can name the marked region rather than a quality, and several flora uses concern vegetation or locality patches.

other_axioms: Normalize the colour-pattern use to PATO:0002274 while preserving the source noun as the evidence span.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0002274 defines multicoloured dappling with spots, patches, or blotches.
counterexample_or_caveat: Do not use for non-colour material heterogeneity unless the different colours are stated or visually entailed.

definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being divided, at least partially, by incisions into visibly distinct segments.
other_axioms: Compare with PATO:0001979 lobed before fixing asserted parentage; dissected requires segment-forming divisions but the available glossary does not impose one universal incision-depth threshold.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has lobed and cleft but no dissected class; the Saudi uses describe leaves or leaf-like structures divided into segments.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some floras reserve dissected for deep divisions and others use it broadly. The proposal deliberately avoids an invented fractional-depth boundary and should not be made equivalent to lobed.

definition: A flora phenotype affecting the leaves borne by one plant or shoot system at a specified time, considered collectively.
other_axioms: Create a FLOPO-local support class foliage directly under PO:0025131 plant anatomical entity, not PO:0025497 collective plant structure, and place a new foliage phenotype branch under the proposed plant-material-aggregate phenotype branch. Require leaf members but do not require spatial adjacency or anatomical connectedness.
current_ontology_status: PO:0009025 uses foliage leaf for one vascular leaf, whereas the surface foliage denotes a collection. PO:0025497 requires adjacent organs, so the distributed collection and its phenotype branch are intentionally developed inside FLOPO.
counterexample_or_caveat: Foliage is temporally indexed and may be distributed across a whole plant or shoot. A generic has_part some leaf axiom is necessary but not sufficient, and a membership relation must be selected before an equivalence axiom is released.

other_axioms: Use decreased size only when a reference population is established; do not map naturally small or horticultural dwarf growth forms to PATO:0000969 dwarf-like, whose definition requires abnormal smallness.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrences describe naturally small herbs and shrubs; PATO:0000969 is explicitly abnormal and therefore not an exact lexical target.
counterexample_or_caveat: Dwarf can denote a taxon, cultivar class, naturally low habit, pathological growth reduction, or relative size. Those senses require different assertions.

definition: A phenotype in which a plant obtains resources through a parasitic relationship to an explicitly identified host organism.
other_axioms: Bind parasite and host as separate organisms and represent the ecological relation; assert a haustorium part only when the description or taxon evidence establishes one.
current_ontology_status: PO contains haustorium but PO and PATO do not supply an atomic quality equivalent to being parasitic; the relation belongs in a contextual phenotype assertion.
counterexample_or_caveat: Host can occur in habitat or taxonomic prose, and not every resource-parasitic interaction described at species level licenses an observed haustorium for the individual.

definition: A phenotype assertion that relates one explicitly identified plant structure to another by origin, support, coverage, production, or relative attachment.
other_axioms: Parse the complete predicate and both PO arguments before selecting develops_from, has_part, part_of, adjacent_to, or a more specific relation; do not normalize isolated participles as qualities.
current_ontology_status: The corpus spans are fragments of relational constructions such as arising from, subtended by, covered with, and bearing structures.
counterexample_or_caveat: The verbs are not interchangeable: a bract subtending a flower is not necessarily part of it, and a structure arising near another need not develop from it.

other_axioms: Reject corpus occurrences in coral-rock, coral-limestone, and fossil-coral habitat descriptions; retain any future explicitly chromatic coral-coloured construction for separate colour evidence.
current_ontology_status: The inspected Saudi uses describe geological substrate rather than plant colour.
counterexample_or_caveat: Coral is also a conventional colour name in other contexts, so this is a construction-specific rejection rather than a global lexical ban.

other_axioms: Normalize bearer-bound arrangements in one or more rings around an axis to PATO:0001951; keep the noun phrase and identified organ count in the phenotype assertion.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001951 already represents the whorled arrangement quality and PlantNET defines a whorl as a ring of organs at one axis level.
counterexample_or_caveat: A whorl is the group of organs while whorled is the arrangement quality; this lexical mapping must not erase the bearer or turn every ring-shaped object into a whorl.

other_axioms: Resolve Fabaceae wing petals to their PO entity and fruit, seed, stem, petiole, or rachis flanges to the applicable organ part; use the PATO winged quality only when homology is unspecified.
current_ontology_status: PlantNET explicitly separates wing-petal and flange senses; PO already has wing petal, while the generic surface form does not determine which structure is present.
counterexample_or_caveat: Collapsing all wings into one PO class would conflate non-homologous structures. The singular corpus use is also syntactically ambiguous.

definition: A phenotype assertion that compares a specified morphological attribute of a plant structure with an explicit or discourse-supplied reference.
other_axioms: Bind the PO bearer, PATO attribute, direction, and comparison target; retain modifiers such as -ish as uncertainty and do not coerce superlatives into absolute qualities.
current_ontology_status: The isolated forms omit at least the attribute or reference required by PATO's increased/decreased values; several are local comparisons among organ parts.
counterexample_or_caveat: Darker may concern colour lightness rather than saturation, wider is usually numeric or relational, and narrowed can describe shape change rather than decreased width.

other_axioms: Use the caespitose whole-plant proposal only for basal shoot clumps; otherwise bind the repeated entity and represent its clustered arrangement; never normalize the generic noun to PO:0020061 coma unless it is specifically a seed-micropyle trichome tuft.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include tufts of hairs, anthers, or appendages as well as whole-plant clumping, so the noun is not an exact synonym of caespitose or of the seed-specific PO coma.
counterexample_or_caveat: A tuft is a cluster configuration whose members and bearer must be stated; it is not itself a bearer-independent quality.

definition: The above-ground portion of a tree shoot system comprising the branches and foliage above the lowest principal branch.
other_axioms: Promote the current NARROW synonym tree crown on shoot system to an explicit subclass; map crown only when the tree architecture sense is established.
current_ontology_status: PO:0009006 has tree crown as a NARROW synonym but no corresponding subclass.
counterexample_or_caveat: Corpus uses also describe floral crowns, open crown shapes, shoot branching sites, and host locations; those senses must not map to the tree-crown entity.

other_axioms: Use PO:0025518 for angular projections on a leaf margin and PO:0025515 for a phyllome-lamina tooth; keep non-laminar stem or fruit projections as separate shape/entity descriptions.
current_ontology_status: PO already defines phyllome and leaf lamina teeth, including the plural exact synonym for leaf lamina teeth.
counterexample_or_caveat: The corpus also calls succulent stem projections teeth. A surface-only mapping to leaf anatomy would therefore be wrong.

definition: A phenotype assertion that relates a specified plant structure or whole plant to a developmental stage or directional change over time.
other_axioms: Bind the bearer and stage or process; map enlarging to increased size only when the changing attribute is size and retain senescence, death, and development as processes or stages rather than static atomic qualities.
current_ontology_status: These participles occur in temporal descriptions of flowers, fruits, leaves, or plants and do not identify a complete quality by themselves.
counterexample_or_caveat: Colour changes while aging and organ death require the changed attribute and time relation; treating aging itself as a quality would lose that structure.

definition: A shape and orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of its distal portion being curved or bent downward from a more upright supporting axis.
other_axioms: First revise the malformed definition of PATO:0002165 drooping, then consider nodding as its distal-portion subtype; do not equate it with PATO:0104035 pendent, which describes a more fully downward-hanging orientation.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0002165 currently says only 'To bent or hang downwards'; UPOV operationally distinguishes drooping and pendent but does not itself define nodding.
counterexample_or_caveat: The cited source supports the parent contrast, not the complete nodding differentia. This row is deliberately not an accept proposal until a botanical glossary definition is pinned.

definition: A disposition inhering in a plant structure by virtue of the structure remaining attached to its bearer beyond the developmental stage at which structures of that type ordinarily detach.
other_axioms: Revise PATO:0001732, whose current label and definition incorrectly require a plant to shed no body part, into a generic persistent-organ counterpart of PATO:0001730; preserve evergreen plant separately as PATO:0001733.
current_ontology_status: PATO has generic deciduous, deciduous plant, non-deciduous any body part, and evergreen plant, but no correctly defined generic persistent organ quality.
counterexample_or_caveat: Persistence is relative to organ type and developmental stage: persistent sepals do not imply an evergreen plant or a plant that sheds no parts.

other_axioms: Normalize aqueous transported plant sap to PO:0025538; retain resin, gum, latex, and generic exudate as distinct substances.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025538 is current and explicitly warns that plant sap is not latex, resin, or cytoplasm.
counterexample_or_caveat: Flora prose can use sap loosely for exudates; nearby descriptors such as milky do not prove that the substance satisfies PO's transport definition.

definition: A botanical odor description in which an odor is characterized by resemblance to familiar pungent spices.
other_axioms: Map the presence of odor to PATO:0001331 and retain spicy as an unresolved odor-character modifier until a controlled odor vocabulary supplies an operational prototype.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi uses concern scent rather than taste; pinned PATO has odorous but no defined spicy-odor value.
counterexample_or_caveat: Spicy is prototype-based and culture-dependent, and it must not be inferred as a taste, chemical composition, pleasantness, or odor intensity.

definition: A whole-plant ecological phenotype in which the plant grows in water, with its relevant structures submerged below or floating at the water surface as explicitly stated.
other_axioms: Represent aquatic ecology separately from the relational positions submerged and floating; bind the water body and the plant structure whose position is described.
current_ontology_status: Released FLOPO has a whole-plant ecology branch but no reviewed atomic PATO quality that captures the organism-water relation.
counterexample_or_caveat: Aquatic does not entail that every plant part is submerged, and floating can describe detached organs or buoyancy rather than a whole-plant life form.

definition: A relational positional quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of the structure at least partially enclosing an axis to which it is attached.
other_axioms: Add amplexicaul only as a narrow synonym for the stem-clasping botanical use; do not place clasping under PATO:0001772 surrounding, whose definition requires extension on all sides simultaneously.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has surrounding/encircling but no quality for partial enclosure by an attached plant part.
counterexample_or_caveat: Clasping usually concerns a leaf base around a stem, but the quality is bearer-independent only if the enclosed axis remains an explicit relational argument.

definition: A surface texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being covered with a coarse, flour-like powder.
other_axioms: Add farinose and farinaceous as related or exact synonyms only after confirming whether their finer powder boundary overlaps mealy; represent the powder material separately when known.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has texture and coating but no mealy/farinose botanical surface value.
counterexample_or_caveat: PlantNET distinguishes coarse mealy powder from fine farina, so treating mealy and farinose as exact may erase a granularity distinction used by some floras.

other_axioms: Map fused-together plant parts to the relational quality PATO:0000642 with both entities bound; do not treat united as a monadic structural value.
current_ontology_status: PlantNET defines united as fused together and PATO:0000642 already represents fused with another entity.
counterexample_or_caveat: United can mean politically or collectively joined in ordinary prose, and the relation requires a second anatomical argument.

other_axioms: Normalize bearer-bound alternate organ arrangements to PATO:0001932 and retain the repeated organ type and axis.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001932 defines elements placed alternately one above another.
counterexample_or_caveat: Alternate may also express a logical alternative or alternating developmental state; surface matching alone is insufficient.

other_axioms: Use PO:0020046 only for a once-compound palmate leaf; otherwise bind PATO shape or venation topology for palmately lobed, divided, or veined structures.
current_ontology_status: PlantNET separates palmate leaf shape/division and venation uses; PO:0020046 has a narrower compound-leaf definition.
counterexample_or_caveat: An adverb modifying venation or lobing cannot be normalized to the palmate-leaf anatomical class.

definition: A small nipple-like projection produced by or forming part of a plant epidermal cell or surface.
other_axioms: Do not revive obsolete PO:0002001. Map an explicitly cellular bearer to PO:0025166 or its leaf/stigma subclasses; send subcellular papillae to GO and leave multicellular corolla-surface projections unresolved.
current_ontology_status: PO:0002001 papillae is obsolete because its stigma-cell sense was redirected to GO, while PO retains papilla cell classes.
counterexample_or_caveat: Saudi corolla papillae may be multicellular surface projections, so neither a papilla cell nor a GO subcellular component is safe without histological context; the provisional definition lacks sufficient evidence.

other_axioms: Map inward-rolled margins to involute, backward/outward-rolled margins to revolute, and layered folds to folded only after direction and bearer are recovered.
current_ontology_status: PATO already distinguishes folded, involute, and revolute; isolated rolled does not select among them.
counterexample_or_caveat: Rolled petals, leaf margins, and whole laminas differ in geometry, and a rolled organ is not necessarily curled spirally on both sides.

definition: A phenotype describing the distribution of staminate and pistillate reproductive structures within or among flowers, individuals, or populations.
other_axioms: Bind the level of organization before using PO staminate/pistillate flower classes or modeling monoecious, dioecious, and unisexual conditions; do not equate separate with unfused.
current_ontology_status: PlantNET defines unisexual at the reproductive-organ level, while corpus phrases such as sexes separate may concern flowers or different plants.
counterexample_or_caveat: Separate also means physically distinct or unfused in morphology; the isolated token cannot determine reproductive semantics.

other_axioms: Add lax as an exact botanical synonym of PATO:0001802 for non-compact arrangements.
current_ontology_status: PlantNET defines lax as loose or not compact, matching PATO:0001802.
counterexample_or_caveat: Lax can describe posture or physiological tone outside botany; accept only the botanical arrangement sense.

definition: A whole-plant growth phenotype in which shoot axes extend along or close to the ground, with rooting at nodes represented separately when it occurs.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0002389 procumbent only for horizontal growth without rooting; distinguish stoloniferous/rooting axes, unsupported trailing axes, and broadly spreading architecture rather than declaring them exact synonyms.
current_ontology_status: The glossaries distinguish procumbent from stolons that root at nodes; released FLOPO lacks evidence-backed definitions for several growth-form labels.
counterexample_or_caveat: Creeping can imply rooting in some sources but merely low horizontal growth in others, and rooted alone can describe an individual specimen rather than a growth form.

definition: A phenotype assertion that locates or orients a specified plant structure relative to another structure, medium, surface, or coordinate frame.
other_axioms: Recover both relata and direction before selecting a PATO relation; reject habitat uses such as protected desert or road descending, and distinguish occlusion, enclosure, insertion, burial, and below-ground location.
current_ontology_status: The isolated words are incomplete relational predicates, with corpus uses spanning fruits enclosed by calyces, seeds embedded in flesh, organs hidden by petals, structures buried in wool or sand, and locality prose.
counterexample_or_caveat: Enclosed does not entail fused or contained as a proper part, visible/hidden depend on an observer and occluder, and underground applies to the relevant organ rather than automatically to the whole plant.

definition: A phenotype assertion in which a specified plant structure is divided into, composed of, or separates into discrete connected or disconnected portions.
other_axioms: Bind the bearer and resulting parts, and distinguish pre-existing articulations from developmental or dehiscence processes; do not coin one PO segment class spanning stems, fruits, leaves, and inflorescences.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include succulent shoot segments, jointed stems, fruit segments, joints, and fruits splitting at maturity.
counterexample_or_caveat: Segments in different organs are not necessarily homologous, and splitting is a process rather than evidence that every resulting portion is a stable anatomical class.

definition: A boundary region of a plant structure at which that structure is externally exposed or contacts another material entity.
other_axioms: Evaluate whether PO should import or define a generic anatomical-surface boundary; meanwhile bind surface-of to the stated organ and reject water-surface uses.
current_ontology_status: PO has epidermis and organ-specific structures but no generic surface class in the pinned release.
counterexample_or_caveat: A mathematical/anatomical boundary is not automatically a material plant structure, and the corpus also uses surface of water. The proposed category and parent therefore need upper-ontology review.

other_axioms: Map a terminal point or very small terminal region only after the bearer is known; do not make tip an exact synonym of apex, which can denote an extended distal region.
current_ontology_status: PO has several organ-specific tip and apex classes but no safe unrestricted target for the surface word.
counterexample_or_caveat: Tips of leaves, fruits, spines, flower stems, and corolla lobes need different bearer-bound entities, and some occurrences participate in leaf-tip tendril constructions.

other_axioms: Retain fine with its modified hair, line, or texture; treat extreme and rare as degree/frequency evidence; reject taxonomic intermediate form, locality extreme edge, and fresh-water uses outside an individual phenotype.
current_ontology_status: These words either modify another phenotype component or belong to population, taxonomy, or habitat prose.
counterexample_or_caveat: Fine can mean small diameter, narrow marking, or high granularity, while rare is population frequency rather than an organism quality.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure resembles a hair in being slender and elongated without thereby being identified as a trichome.
other_axioms: Use PO:0000282 trichome only when developmental or anatomical context establishes a trichome; otherwise retain resemblance and bind the actual bract, scale, or other structure.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include hair-like bracts and scales, not only true hairs.
counterexample_or_caveat: Shape resemblance does not establish homology, epidermal origin, or the unicellular/multicellular criteria in PO's trichome definition.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified floral organ or group of floral organs forms a concave covering region resembling a hood.
other_axioms: Model the hood-like shape on the explicitly identified petal, sepal, lip, or fused floral region rather than minting one PO hood entity across non-homologous structures.
current_ontology_status: The corpus places a hood in different flowers and sometimes uses quotation marks, indicating a descriptive region rather than a stable homology.
