counterexample_or_caveat: A hood can be formed by one petal or several fused organs; the word alone does not identify the bearer or developmental origin.

other_axioms: Use PO:0020141 when the node is explicitly part of a stem and the broader PO:0005004 otherwise.
current_ontology_status: PO already defines shoot axis node and stem node; Saudi uses concern rooting, hairs, flowers, or swelling at stem nodes.
counterexample_or_caveat: Node is used in other graph and anatomical domains, so the botanical shoot-axis bearer remains necessary.

surface_forms: spire shaped|flat topped|budlike|spike like|star|stars|pea like|pitcher shaped|umbrella shaped|squat
definition: A phenotype in which the shape of a specified plant structure is described by resemblance to a named prototype or by a relative compactness profile.
other_axioms: Retrieve an existing PATO shape only when its operational geometry matches; otherwise preserve the prototype phrase and bearer instead of adding one PATO class for every everyday-object comparison.
current_ontology_status: The terms describe whole-plant habit, flowers, fruits, heads, calyces, or stems by analogy and currently lack uniformly sourced operational boundaries.
counterexample_or_caveat: Prototype resemblance is not homology, and squat is a relative height-to-width judgment requiring a reference; no class in this row is proposed for automatic acceptance.

other_axioms: Reject retaining-wall, rock-wall, bay, stone, and livestock-stock habitat or narrative uses from individual phenotype extraction.
current_ontology_status: The inspected occurrences are localities, substrates, water bodies, or grazing narrative.
counterexample_or_caveat: Stone can describe a fruit endocarp and stock can describe plant material in other corpora, so this rejection is limited to the verified Saudi constructions.

other_axioms: Use pendent for an organ hanging downward and drooping for a bent-downward form only when the plant bearer is explicit; reject locality phrases such as hanging valley.
current_ontology_status: Most Saudi occurrences are habitat/locality prose; one describes hanging roots.
counterexample_or_caveat: The surface form does not distinguish suspension, curvature, or a geographical overhang.

other_axioms: Map compound leaf only when leaf is the bearer; retain compound inflorescence, fruit, and ordinary compositional uses separately.
current_ontology_status: PO:0020043 defines compound leaf, and several Saudi uses explicitly modify leaves.
counterexample_or_caveat: Compound is a structural operator, not an unrestricted synonym of compound leaf.

other_axioms: Use a ridged or raised plant-feature phenotype only when a plant bearer is explicit; reject dune and rocky-spur crest localities.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrences are predominantly topographic.
counterexample_or_caveat: A crest can be an anatomical outgrowth, an inflorescence shape, or the top of a landform; the isolated noun is not a safe ontology class.

definition: A flower that is one of multiple small flowers composing a compact inflorescence or spikelet.
other_axioms: Promote a generic floret subclass only after a botanical definition is pinned; retain PO's existing spikelet-floret descendants and do not classify a solitary small flower as a floret solely by size.
current_ontology_status: PO has taxon- and spikelet-specific floret classes but no generic class matching Asteraceae ray-floret use.
counterexample_or_caveat: The provisional definition combines size and inflorescence membership; different botanical traditions may use floret outside compact inflorescences, so this is not ready for acceptance.

other_axioms: Reject phrases saying that habit is variable or differs; extract the separately stated growth-form descriptors instead.
current_ontology_status: The occurrences are metalinguistic references to overall growth form rather than values such as erect, lax, or bushy.
counterexample_or_caveat: Habit is a legitimate phenotype category, but the category word alone does not assert a value.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure bears or terminates in a curved, pointed, or elongated projection described as a horn or hook.
other_axioms: Bind the projection and bearer; use PATO:0002215 falciform only for genuinely sickle-shaped curvature and do not infer a PO spine, prickle, or horn homology from the nickname.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include fruit horns, cyathium horns, leaf-base horns, and adhesive fruit hooks.
counterexample_or_caveat: PATO currently treats hooked as exactly falciform, but a small attachment hook need not have a full sickle shape, and horn-shaped projections are not homologous across organs.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure lacks the leaves, hairs, bracts, covering, or other structures normally expected in the stated context.
other_axioms: Represent absence of the explicitly recoverable covering or appendage; do not map naked globally to leafless or glabrous.
current_ontology_status: Corpus uses include naked stems and naked parasitic stems, with different omitted structures.
counterexample_or_caveat: The word is elliptical and reference-dependent; a naked stem can be leafless while still hairy, and a naked flower can lack a perianth rather than leaves.

other_axioms: Normalize the flora smell sense to PATO:0001208 odorless; never use PATO:0002192 non-aromatic, which is a molecular ring-structure quality.
current_ontology_status: The corpus contrasts aromatic and nonaromatic plants by smell, while PATO:0001208 represents lacking odor.
counterexample_or_caveat: A specimen described as nonaromatic may still have a non-aromatic-category odor; curator review should decide whether the flora author means fully odorless or merely lacking a notable aroma.

definition: A surface quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having a perceptibly oil-like liquid or greasy coating.
other_axioms: Add only after evidence distinguishes an actual oil coating from glossy appearance, glandular secretion, and tactile greasiness.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses describe oily glandular foliage or a plant oily to touch; PATO has generic liquid coating but no reviewed oily subtype.
counterexample_or_caveat: The description does not establish chemical composition as oil, and the provisional definition lacks a pinned botanical or material-science boundary.

other_axioms: Map tightly packed structures to crowded or condensed and widely spaced structures to uncrowded only with the repeated entity and bearer bound.
current_ontology_status: PATO distinguishes crowded, uncrowded, and condensed, while Saudi phrases supply degree modifiers such as widely and tightly.
counterexample_or_caveat: Physical mass density is not asserted, and packed may describe enclosure rather than a regular spatial pattern.

definition: A trichome phenotype in which the trichome has the disposition to deliver an irritating portion of plant substance to an animal upon contact or breakage.
other_axioms: Create a FLOPO-local stinging disposition under PATO:0001727 and compose it with PO:0000282 trichome; add stinging hair as an exact synonym of the phenotype. Do not classify the trichome under PO:0004509 glandular trichome or universally assert a lumen without additional evidence.
current_ontology_status: PO supplies the anatomical bearer and FLOPO:0000355 supplies its phenotype branch, but the corpus needs the bearer-plus-disposition phenotype rather than a new PO anatomical kind.
counterexample_or_caveat: PlantNET describes a hollow hair seated on a secreting gland. This supports the delivery disposition and trichome bearer, but it does not show that every stinging trichome satisfies PO's glandular-trichome differentia.

definition: A structural quality inhering in a slender bearer by virtue of the bearer being tough and capable of bending without readily breaking.
other_axioms: Seek a botanical glossary definition and compare with flexible, tough, slender, and filiform before acceptance.
current_ontology_status: All Saudi uses describe slender black fern stems; PATO has flexible but no evidence-backed wiry composite.
counterexample_or_caveat: Wiry jointly conveys diameter, toughness, and flexibility, so it may be better modeled compositionally than as one atomic PATO quality.

other_axioms: Map quoted botanical wool to lanate only when it denotes a covering of long tangled trichomes; otherwise retain the actual hair cluster or fibrous material.
current_ontology_status: The descriptions use wool metaphorically for masses of white hairs around flowers or fruits.
counterexample_or_caveat: A noun naming accumulated hairs is not automatically the same as the bearer's lanate pilosity quality, and some woolly masses may be short, dense, or papery rather than lanate.

definition: A ring-shaped plant structure or region surrounding another floral structure.
other_axioms: Do not map to PO growth ring; bind the corolla or corona bearer and determine whether the annulus is a ridge, hair ring, disc, or other tissue before proposing an anatomical subclass.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include a raised ring encircling a corona and a hairy corolla annulus; PO has no generic floral-annulus class.
counterexample_or_caveat: The two structures need not be homologous or even the same material category, so the provisional label is a surface grouping rather than an accept proposal.

definition: A phenotype assertion specifying the spatial organization of repeated plant structures relative to an axis, level, side, or one another.
other_axioms: Parse the complete construction before selecting alternate, whorled, opposite, spiral, paired, ranked, or clustered pattern values.
current_ontology_status: The verb introduces an arrangement but does not itself state which arrangement applies.
counterexample_or_caveat: Normalizing arranged as a quality would discard the actual pattern expressed later in the sentence.

definition: A texture and composition quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of the bearer being thin, dry, and membranous like a chaff scale or bract.
other_axioms: Compare with scarious and membranous terminology and decide whether resemblance to chaff should remain a FLOPO composition rather than one atomic PATO quality.
current_ontology_status: PlantNET defines chaff as membranous scales or bracts and glumaceous as chaffy or membranous; the Saudi bearer is a bract.
counterexample_or_caveat: The sources do not state that every chaffy structure is simultaneously thin, dry, and membranous, so this composed differentia is not yet an accept proposal.

other_axioms: Use strobilus only when reproductive sporophyll or ovule-bearing anatomy is established; map male cone to microsporangiate strobilus and female cone to megasporangiate strobilus only in the applicable botanical sense.
current_ontology_status: PO carries cone as a related term for strobilus and male/female cone as related synonyms on the two sexed strobilus classes.
counterexample_or_caveat: Saudi cone-shaped bodies and quoted cones sometimes merely describe clustered bracts or fruits, so the related scope is justified and must not be promoted by string alone.

other_axioms: Normalize a smoothly bending plant organ to curved while preserving directional modifiers such as upward or backward.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000406 defines a curve or smoothly rounded bend.
counterexample_or_caveat: Curving can describe an ongoing change rather than a static form, and direction must remain in the phenotype assertion.

other_axioms: Use plant deciduous PATO:0001731 for whole-plant foliage shedding, generic deciduous PATO:0001730 for a stated organ, and evergreen plant PATO:0001733 for foliage retention.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO distinguishes generic and plant deciduous from evergreen plant; the glossaries support the botanical meanings.
counterexample_or_caveat: A deciduous flower spike is not a deciduous plant, and evergreen does not mean that no organ is ever shed.

other_axioms: Use the existing fringed quality only for a bearer with a border of hair-like or finger-like projections; reject village-fringe and field-fringe locality uses.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001989 is the candidate used by the existing fringed proposal, while the Saudi noun occurs in both anatomy and locality prose.
counterexample_or_caveat: The noun can name the border itself rather than the bearer's quality, so entity-to-quality coercion requires a bearer.

definition: A shape quality inhering in a woody bearer by virtue of the bearer having an irregular, twisted form with conspicuous knots or contortions.
other_axioms: Find a dendrological definition that separates gnarled shape from rough bark, branching complexity, and age before acceptance.
current_ontology_status: All Saudi occurrences describe old-looking tree trunks or whole trees; pinned PATO has no gnarled value.
counterexample_or_caveat: The provisional definition combines independent form and surface features and may be taxon- or age-dependent.

definition: A curation group for botanical colour descriptors whose individual members are recognized against a named physical chip, Munsell notation, or botanical exemplar specified by a cited standard.
other_axioms: Split the group using curation/botanical_colour_prototypes.tsv. Source-qualified lemon-yellow, mahogany-red, salmon, chocolate-brown, and straw-yellow can receive operational proposals; chestnut, olive, and rose require sense/source splits; golden and silvery include lustre and remain FLOPO appearance compositions unless a pure colour standard is explicit.
current_ontology_status: Saccardo supplies botanical exemplars and plates; Ridgway supplies named chips with Hamly Munsell approximations; RHS/UPOV demonstrates the modern chip-based method. The Saudi flora does not declare that it used any of these standards.
counterexample_or_caveat: A prototype defines the standard-qualified concept, not every unqualified occurrence. Olive and rose are often resemblance or taxonomic prose, natural-object exemplars vary, historical plates age, and Hamly advises using its conversion for legacy interpretation rather than new observations.

other_axioms: Normalize the primary-axis sense to PO:0009047, whose definition already states that a stem is the primary axis of a plant.
current_ontology_status: PO:0009047 makes main stem lexically redundant in the observed sense.
counterexample_or_caveat: Some plants have multiple co-dominant stems; use the mapping only where the description identifies the primary axis.

definition: A folded quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer being folded back and forth longitudinally like a fan.
other_axioms: Add pleated only as a related synonym because ordinary pleating need not be longitudinal; preserve the repeated longitudinal-fold differentia relative to generic folded.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO has folded but no plicate subtype; both pinned glossaries give the longitudinal-fold criterion.
counterexample_or_caveat: A single longitudinal fold is not necessarily plicate if it does not alternate back and forth; the Flora of Australia wording supplies that stricter boundary.

other_axioms: Bind the PO spine entity when homology is known; otherwise use the broad spiny quality and model spineless as qualified absence, retaining soft, stout, and tipped modifiers on the actual spine or bearer.
current_ontology_status: The corpus includes leaf, stipular, stem, and succulent armature plus absence and modifier phrases.
counterexample_or_caveat: Botanical spines have different developmental origins, and PATO spiny does not identify which organ bears them.

other_axioms: Use compact clustered-flower composition for an inflorescence, globose shape for a stigma, and rounded-apical-cell shape for a hair; do not coin one atomic value spanning all three.
current_ontology_status: The official glossaries explicitly define separate inflorescence, stigma, and hair senses.
counterexample_or_caveat: The Saudi occurrences modify flower heads and do not justify a universal head-shaped quality on every bearer called capitate.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant surface contains an opening, groove, fissure, or depressed region of stated shape and depth.
other_axioms: Bind the plant bearer and select a PATO concavity, groove, or fissure only when the occurrence is anatomical; reject rock cracks, sand depressions, water-holes, and volcanic blow-holes.
current_ontology_status: Most singular crack, depression, and hole uses are habitat prose, while fissured bark and one trunk crack are genuine plant morphology.
counterexample_or_caveat: These features differ topologically and quantitatively, so the grouping is an extraction decision, not a proposed common ontology class.

other_axioms: Map crisped to curled in the pinned glossary sense and crinkled leaves to wrinkled only when their creases, rather than marginal curl, are described.
current_ontology_status: Flora of Australia defines crisped as curled; PATO already has curled and wrinkled.
counterexample_or_caveat: Crinkled may combine small folds, wrinkles, and curl, so an unrestricted exact synonym of wrinkled is not proposed.

other_axioms: Map elongate to elongated, tapering to tapered, bifurcate to bifurcated, and dome shaped to domed after recovering the bearer.
current_ontology_status: Pinned PATO contains all four candidate values.
counterexample_or_caveat: Morphological inflection is safe only after word sense, and bifurcate appears in an OCR-damaged phrase whose bearer must be recovered.

definition: A phenotype in which a non-petal plant structure resembles a petal by having soft texture and conspicuous colour.
other_axioms: Compose texture and an explicitly stated or prototype-backed colour on the identified PO bearer; do not create one atomic PATO class or identify the bearer as a petal.
current_ontology_status: The glossary defines petaloid through both texture and colour; the Saudi bearer is a sepal or appendage.
counterexample_or_caveat: Petal resemblance does not establish homology, and conspicuous colour still needs its actual value when available.

surface_forms: triangular in cross section|cross section|two lipped
preferred_label: contextual section or bilabiate shape phenotype
definition: A phenotype describing either the shape of a specified transverse section or a floral structure divided into two lip-like regions.
other_axioms: Compose triangular cross section with PATO:0001875 on the section, and model bilabiate/two-lipped corollas only after the fused anterior and posterior organ groups are identified.
current_ontology_status: PATO has triangular, while Flora of Australia defines bilabiate through two fused groups of corolla parts.
counterexample_or_caveat: The cross section is a fiat/reference region rather than automatically a PO organ, and two-lipped morphology can be formed by different floral organs.

definition: A reproductive phenotype in which seed is formed without sexual fusion of gametes.
other_axioms: Link the applicable plant reproductive process to the whole plant or taxon and retain the source's explanatory statement; do not normalize reproduction or fusion in isolation as PATO structural qualities.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi text itself explicitly defines apomictic in these terms, but no independent scientific source is yet pinned for an ontology proposal.
counterexample_or_caveat: Apomixis has multiple developmental mechanisms, and this occurrence is family-level narrative rather than a direct observation of one specimen.

definition: A plant structure that projects from or is attached to a larger plant structure.
other_axioms: Do not add a generic class until PO curators decide whether it has a coherent anatomical differentia; map the corpus petaloid appendage to its actual cyathium structure when recoverable.
current_ontology_status: PO definitions use the ordinary word appendage but the pinned ontology has no generic plant-appendage class.
counterexample_or_caveat: The provisional definition is merely relational and groups non-homologous organs and organ parts, so it is not ready for acceptance.

definition: A whole-plant growth phenotype in which a non-tree plant or shrub develops a tree-like stature or architecture.
other_axioms: Represent resemblance to the tree growth form without inferring that the bearer is a tree anatomical entity.
current_ontology_status: Flora of Australia explicitly applies arborescent to non-woody plants attaining tree height and shrubs tending toward tree-like size.
counterexample_or_caveat: Tree-like is still a prototype comparison and may concern height, a single main stem, or crown architecture; the source supports the broad growth phenotype, not all of those components universally.

other_axioms: Reject the verified OCR/tokenization fragments: lowers is flowers missing its initial letter, tri is part of tri-lobed, ate occurs in corrupt text, pores is stray page noise, and discolor is a taxon epithet.
current_ontology_status: None of these isolated spans is a phenotype value in the source context.
counterexample_or_caveat: The correctly spelled complete words can be meaningful elsewhere; rejection applies only to the verified spans and should feed OCR repair rules.

definition: A leaf phenotype in which the bearer is a compound leaf with exactly two leaflets.
other_axioms: Place under leaf phenotype and the proposed composition/cardinality facet, assert has_part exactly 2 PO:0020049, and associate it with a FLOPO-local bifoliolate quality under PATO:0001555.
current_ontology_status: PO supplies compound leaf and leaflet but need not coin every leaflet-count combination; the compositional phenotype and supporting value are intentionally local to FLOPO.
counterexample_or_caveat: The exact cardinality concerns ultimate leaflets; two primary divisions that are themselves divided do not satisfy the proposed definition.

definition: A colour phenotype combining the operational orange-red colour value with explicitly increased brightness relative to the relevant comparison.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0104112 orange red for the prototype-backed hue component and preserve bright as a contextual lightness/brightness modifier; do not mint another atomic colour without an operational brightness boundary.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0104112 has an RHS Colour Chart prototype and occurs in the current checked-in PATO source.
counterexample_or_caveat: Bright lacks a stated comparison or numeric lightness range in the flora description, so only the orange-red component is eligible for deterministic normalization.

definition: A bark phenotype in which the bearer has a conspicuous cork-rich, thickened, or cork-like outer surface.
other_axioms: Bind PO bark and retain corky as unresolved composition until an anatomical or texture definition distinguishes cork tissue abundance from mere resemblance.
current_ontology_status: The sole Saudi use is corky-barked vine; no pinned glossary in the evidence set defines corky.
counterexample_or_caveat: Appearance does not prove chemical or tissue composition, and the provisional wording presents alternatives rather than a sufficient differentia.

definition: A phenotype in which a bearer has an odor characterized by an explicitly stated prototype or hedonic descriptor.
other_axioms: Map odor presence to PATO:0001331 and retain foul or balsam-like character as source evidence; do not infer chemical composition, taste, or a universal pleasantness scale.
current_ontology_status: The corpus uses foul smelling fruit, sweet-smelling flesh, and balsam-like aroma; PATO has odorous but no supported prototype classes for these character words.
counterexample_or_caveat: Hedonic judgments and prototype resemblance vary among observers, so new atomic PATO values require controlled definitions and evaluation.

definition: A flora phenotype affecting plant latex, where plant latex is the cytoplasmic fluid of laticifer cells, commonly containing particles suspended or emulsified in an aqueous phase and capable of exuding when laticiferous tissue is damaged.
other_axioms: Create a FLOPO-local plant latex support class under PO:0025161 portion of plant substance and use it to define and extend the existing FLOPO:0900048 latex phenotype branch. Keep it distinct from PO:0025538 plant sap; do not make universal colour, milkiness, stickiness, or post-exudation-location axioms.
current_ontology_status: FLOPO:0900048--0900051 already provide an undeveloped latex phenotype/presence branch. The literature defines in-situ latex through laticifer cells, and PlantNET supplies the field-recognition criterion after cutting.
counterexample_or_caveat: Latex composition and appearance vary. A strict part_of some laticifer-cell axiom would fail for already exuded latex, so containment should be stated temporally in text or modeled with a relation that permits former containment.

definition: A plant exudate that becomes sticky or viscous at the exposed plant surface.
other_axioms: Find a pharmacognostic or botanical definition separating gum, resin, latex, mucilage, and sap before proposing a PO class.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrence describes a very sticky gum, but the pinned evidence set does not define the substance.
counterexample_or_caveat: Stickiness is a quality and does not by itself establish the chemical or anatomical identity of gum.

other_axioms: Use actinomorphic for radially symmetric flowers and zygomorphic for flowers divisible into symmetric halves in only one longitudinal plane when the flora's regular/irregular terminology clearly has that sense.
current_ontology_status: PATO already defines both botanical symmetry values; the Saudi text uses regular and irregular in family-level explanatory prose.
counterexample_or_caveat: Irregular need not always mean bilaterally symmetric, and regular has ordinary non-symmetry senses; no exact lexical synonym is proposed.

other_axioms: Use inflexible for a leaf described as rigid, retaining pointed shape separately.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001545 defines inability to bend or twist without breaking and has stiff as an exact synonym.
counterexample_or_caveat: Rigid can also mean geometrically fixed or hard under pressure; the mapping is specific to the botanical flexibility sense.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure bears one or more elongated raised ridges, with keeled structures additionally folded and ridged along a midline.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0002358 ridged for the generic raised feature; propose keeled only as the conjunction of folded and midline-ridged conditions, and retain the noun ridge as the feature rather than automatically coercing it to a quality.
current_ontology_status: Flora of Australia defines keel as a ridge and keeled leaves, petals, or bracts as folded and ridged along the midrib; it equates costate with ribbed.
counterexample_or_caveat: A boat-shaped Fabaceae keel is an anatomical petal complex, not merely the keeled quality, and rib number/orientation is not specified by generic ridged.

other_axioms: Use vestigial only when the spine is a remnant structure from development or evolution; otherwise model decreased size or incomplete development without asserting evolutionary history.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000588 has the closest existing meaning, while the Saudi occurrence describes very small rudimentary spines.
counterexample_or_caveat: Every small or poorly developed structure is not vestigial, and the flora description does not state evolutionary loss of function.

definition: A leaf phenotype in which a leaf resembles a needle or scale in explicitly recoverable shape and size characteristics without being identified as a non-leaf structure.
other_axioms: Bind the leaf entity and preserve resemblance; map to an existing PATO acicular or scale-like shape only if its definition matches the observed geometry.
current_ontology_status: The source phrases already identify the bearers as leaves.
counterexample_or_caveat: Needle-like and scale-like are prototype descriptions, not evidence that the leaf is a needle, scale, or particular taxonomic leaf subtype.

other_axioms: Normalize the floral-organ sense to PO:0009072.
current_ontology_status: PO defines the basal carpel or fused-carpel region enclosing ovules, matching the Saudi context.
counterexample_or_caveat: Ovary is an animal homonym outside botanical context, and nearby pointed-oval wording must not be parsed as part of the label.

other_axioms: Use PO:0020104 for the lower leaf part encasing a stem; retain salt sheath and generic rolled/tubular coverings as material or contextual structures.
current_ontology_status: PO and both glossaries define leaf sheath, but one Saudi occurrence is a sheath of exuded salt rather than anatomy.
counterexample_or_caveat: The bare word does not establish that the structure is part of a vascular leaf.

other_axioms: Map stipules to PO:0020041 and interpret stipular as a relational modifier meaning borne by or derived from a stipule, preserving the modified spine or thorn.
current_ontology_status: PO and PlantNET define stipule as an appendage at the leaf base.
counterexample_or_caveat: A stipular thorn may be a modified stipule, but the adjective alone does not license identity without the anatomical context.

definition: A whole-plant phenotype that constrains the number or conspicuous presence of stem axes.
other_axioms: Bind PO stem and represent many-stemmed cardinality or qualified stem absence/reduction; do not assert literal absence when a stemless plant has a highly reduced or subterranean stem.
current_ontology_status: The corpus uses many-stemmed and usually stemless as growth-habit descriptions.
counterexample_or_caveat: Many has no fixed numeric boundary, and stemless can mean acaulescent rather than anatomically lacking every stem.

definition: A population- or stand-level phenotype in which multiple plant individuals or densely interwoven shoots occupy a localized area.
other_axioms: Route colony formation and thicket growth to population/ecology annotation, distinguishing clonal ramets from separate individuals and a single highly branched plant.
current_ontology_status: Saudi descriptions say plants grow or sucker in colonies and shrubs form dense thickets.
counterexample_or_caveat: The unit of observation is often above the individual-plant level, so these assertions must not be attached to one whole plant without resolving genet/ramet structure.

other_axioms: Use the corolla-tube proposal only when the bearer is fused petals; retain other tubes, inflation regions, and ordinary geometric tubular qualities separately.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi fragments concern a corolla tube or a portion of a tubular flower, but the isolated noun does not state homology.
counterexample_or_caveat: A hollow cylindrical region can be formed by sepals, petals, tepals, stamens, or non-floral organs.

other_axioms: Use banded only for transverse colour rings and surrounding for structures encircling a bearer; the Saudi occurrence says leaves are ringed by dead leaf bases and is relational rather than a colour pattern.
current_ontology_status: Existing PATO candidates cover distinct colour-pattern and positional senses.
counterexample_or_caveat: Ringed does not specify whether the ring is a separate structure, marking, scar, or arrangement.

preferred_label: contextual ranked or paired arrangement phenotype
definition: A phenotype arranging repeated botanical structures in a specified number of longitudinal rows or in a pair.
other_axioms: Bind the repeated PO entity, bearer, and exact count; represent two-ranked and paired constructions rather than normalizing rank or twin in isolation.
current_ontology_status: The corpus describes four leaves in two ranks and twin leaflets.
counterexample_or_caveat: Rank can be taxonomic outside this construction, and twin does not state whether the paired structures are homologous, fused, or merely adjacent.

other_axioms: Use PATO:0001361 when a bearer is covered with hard rough wart-like projections; preserve an individual wart as a surface-feature entity mention.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001361 already defines the bearer-level warty texture and the Saudi occurrences describe raised warts or wart-like glands.
counterexample_or_caveat: A gland resembling a wart need not have the hard rough texture in PATO's definition, so that occurrence remains a resemblance composition.

definition: A colour phenotype in which a specified bearer gradually changes toward, or has a weak admixture of, an explicitly named colour.
other_axioms: Bind both colours and the affected region; model shading as a gradient and tinged as a low-extent admixture without inventing an atomic PATO term for every combination.
current_ontology_status: Saudi phrases include greenish shading to chestnut and white tinged with pink.
counterexample_or_caveat: Neither word supplies a colour value by itself, and tinged does not establish a universal proportion or spatial pattern.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure or marking is oriented perpendicular to the principal longitudinal axis of its bearer.
other_axioms: Bind the bearer axis and the transverse stripe or structure; use PATO:0001946 only when the transverse feature is a colour stripe.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrence modifies black stripes across corolla lobes.
counterexample_or_caveat: Transverse is an orientation relation, not a colour or stripe class by itself.

surface_forms: bright yellow|bright green|bright blue|bright red|bright pink|bright magenta|bright brown|bright purple|bright orange|vivid|dull|whitish|brilliant
preferred_label: contextual colour lightness and chroma phenotype
definition: A colour phenotype in which an operational base colour is modified by a context-dependent description of lightness, chroma, or proximity to that colour.
other_axioms: Retain the base PATO colour and the modifier separately; do not equate bright or brilliant universally with saturated, dull universally with low saturation, or whitish with white without an operational range or prototype.
current_ontology_status: PATO carries the bright-colour phrases only as RELATED synonyms of saturated colours, vivid as RELATED to high saturation, dull as RELATED to low saturation, and whitish as RELATED to white.
counterexample_or_caveat: Brightness can reflect luminance, chroma, or both, and whitish denotes proximity rather than identity. This row deliberately creates no atomic colour and supplies no invented numeric bounds.

definition: A phenotype in which the odor of a specified bearer has relatively increased or decreased perceived intensity in an explicit comparison context.
other_axioms: Use PATO:0001893 increased odor and PATO:0001892 decreased odor for smell constructions; reject the lexical candidates non-fragile and inconspicuous in those contexts and retain non-odor strong/faint senses separately.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrences overwhelmingly modify scent, smell, or aroma, often with prototype character such as sweet, sour, or garlic.
counterexample_or_caveat: Strong also describes thorns or degree and faint can describe colour markings; both values are relative and observer-dependent.

other_axioms: Normalize standard or standard petal to PO:0025324 when it is the upper petal of a papilionaceous corolla; retain the current BROAD synonym scope for unrestricted lexical retrieval.
current_ontology_status: All Saudi occurrences concern Fabaceae flowers and match PO's banner-petal definition.
counterexample_or_caveat: Standard is highly polysemous outside the organ context, and a surface-only global exact synonym would create false mappings.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified plant structure is separated by incisions into lobes, segments, or parts to a stated depth or degree.
other_axioms: Use the dissected proposal, PATO lobed, or an organ-specific PO segmentation only after the bearer and incision depth are recovered; do not map botanical divided leaves automatically to PATO:0001786 split.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses concern partly, finely, or deeply divided petals, leaves, and fronds.
counterexample_or_caveat: PATO split can imply separation into pieces, while a divided lamina may remain one connected organ; degree modifiers carry essential semantics.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified whole plant or arrangement occupies relatively little space because its parts are closely grouped.
other_axioms: Use PATO condensed only for a structure whose parts are closely packed; retain whole-plant compact habit as a FLOPO growth-form composition with its comparison context.
current_ontology_status: PATO treats compact as BROAD for condensed, and Saudi uses describe compact bushy herbs or shrublets.
counterexample_or_caveat: Compact whole-plant habit may result from short internodes, dense branching, or small stature and does not entail one specific structural mechanism.

other_axioms: Use conspicuous only where distinct means clearly visible; otherwise retain a structural-differentiation assertion such as a distinct petiole, keel, stalk, or knob.
current_ontology_status: PATO has distinct only as RELATED to conspicuous, and corpus uses often mean separately discernible anatomical regions rather than visually prominent colour.
counterexample_or_caveat: Two regions can be structurally distinct without either being conspicuous, so the related scope must not be upgraded globally.

other_axioms: Use dappled for small chromatically different specks, spotted for round colour marks, and punctate only when dots, pits, punctures, or points are asserted without necessarily being chromatic.
current_ontology_status: PATO marks speckled RELATED to dappled and dotted RELATED to punctate; Saudi occurrences are mainly coloured specks and dots.
counterexample_or_caveat: The same surface can denote a colour pattern or structural punctures, and the noun-to-bearer pattern coercion requires a host structure.

definition: A thickened or raised region on a floral organ, especially a labellum, that is developmentally part of that organ.
other_axioms: Do not map to PO:0005052 plant callus, which is undifferentiated tissue; find an orchid or floral-morphology source and determine whether calli across floral organs are homologous before proposing a class.
current_ontology_status: All Saudi occurrences describe a coloured callus on a floral lip; they do not describe wound or culture callus tissue.
counterexample_or_caveat: The provisional definition may group independently evolved thickenings and gives no histological criterion, so it remains a PO gap proposal rather than an accepted mapping.

definition: A phenotype relating a plant process, flowering event, or developmental stage to an earlier or later time than an explicit seasonal, daily, or population reference.
other_axioms: Model early morning, early spring, and late afternoon as clock or season context; use PATO premature or delayed only when abnormal developmental timing relative to a stated norm is actually asserted.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi uses are normal phenological timing expressions, not pathology or delayed development.
counterexample_or_caveat: Early and late have no meaning without a temporal reference and must not be normalized to PATO:0000694 or PATO:0000502 merely by related-synonym lookup.

other_axioms: Use PO canal when the occurrence denotes a surface groove or internal tube in a plant structure; retain a purely PATO grooved texture when no anatomical space is intended.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025132 explicitly includes surface grooves and internal tubes, and the Saudi anatomical occurrence is a deep fruit groove.
counterexample_or_caveat: Channel and groove can describe habitat waterways or a shallow surface pattern rather than a discrete anatomical space.

other_axioms: Use leaf midvein for a vascular leaf and costa for the central strand of a non-vascular leaf; do not choose between them without the bearer taxon or leaf type.
current_ontology_status: PO deliberately makes mid rib BROAD on both classes because the common word spans vascular and non-vascular leaves.
counterexample_or_caveat: Costa also has other botanical senses, and the two target classes differ in tissue and bearer.

other_axioms: Use rhizome only when the structure is a swollen horizontal shoot axis producing shoots and roots; retain root crown, woody base, and horticultural graft-stock senses separately.
current_ontology_status: Saudi occurrences describe creeping rootstocks and plausibly denote rhizomes; PO keeps rootstock RELATED rather than exact.
counterexample_or_caveat: A rootstock need not be swollen or a shoot axis in every botanical usage, so lexical promotion would overstate PO's definition.

definition: A phenotype in which exactly two instances of a specified botanical structure occur as a contextually associated pair.
other_axioms: Bind the repeated PO entity and bearer; do not use PATO:0040024 bilaterally paired unless the bilateral/comparative-organism semantics in its definition are satisfied.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include paired spines and paired structures without stating the unusual unpaired-comparator condition in PATO:0040024.
counterexample_or_caveat: A pair need not be bilateral, opposite, homologous, or unusual relative to a comparable organism.

other_axioms: Map free petals to the relational quality unfused from with the other petals or organ group bound; reject PATO:0002316 autogenous, whose definition concerns separate skeletal elements.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrence explicitly contrasts free petals with fused floral structures.
counterexample_or_caveat: Free has many non-structural senses and the relation requires the entity from which the petal is unfused.

other_axioms: Normalize the plant-surface sense to glabrous while preserving the actual bearer.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0000453 represents lacking hairs, and the Saudi occurrence describes an almost hairless fruit.
counterexample_or_caveat: Almost is a degree/exception modifier and prevents an unqualified glabrous assertion unless the extraction preserves that uncertainty.

definition: A dry outer covering of a fruit or seed that remains after removal of its internal contents.
other_axioms: Do not map the Saudi fruit container to PO:0009054 inflorescence bract; find a carpological definition and resolve pericarp, rind, shell, and bract-derived husk senses before proposing a PO class.
current_ontology_status: The occurrence concerns the emptied outer covering of Citrullus fruit, not a maize ear or inflorescence bract.
counterexample_or_caveat: Husk is polysemous and can be pericarp-derived, bract-derived, or a loose seed covering; the provisional definition is functional rather than homologous.

other_axioms: Reject the family-level phrase a large number of species from individual phenotype extraction; retain numeric cardinalities only when a botanical bearer is explicitly counted.
current_ontology_status: The sole occurrence is taxonomic narrative.
counterexample_or_caveat: Number is an attribute in other contexts, but the surface word alone supplies neither a count nor a phenotype bearer.

other_axioms: Reject among-grass habitat uses; retain grass-like leaf or whole-plant descriptions as resemblance evidence and bind their actual PO bearer without treating grass as an anatomical entity.
current_ontology_status: The surface appears inside both grass habitat phrases and grass-like morphology; neither requires a new PO or PATO class.
counterexample_or_caveat: Grass is a taxonomic/common-name category, while grass-like is a contextual resemblance that can concern leaves, stems, or whole plants.

other_axioms: Repair or reject OCR-separated widespread and hyphenated wide-spread population-distribution constructions; do not map them to PATO spreading.
current_ontology_status: Both Saudi occurrences describe geographic frequency and distribution, not the orientation of a plant or its organs.
counterexample_or_caveat: A correctly parsed spread growth-habit verb in another context would require separate review.

definition: A plant structure that closes or covers an opening of another plant structure and can be displaced or opened to expose it.
other_axioms: Treat the Saudi pitcher-flower lid as a context-bound region until its organ identity is established; compare operculum terminology and do not infer homology from quotation marks.
current_ontology_status: PO has no generic lid class in the pinned release, and the flora description does not identify whether the lid is petal, sepal, corolla lobe, or another region.
counterexample_or_caveat: The provisional functional definition spans non-homologous covers and therefore is not an accept proposal.

other_axioms: Parse rough-textured as a complete construction and normalize the stated rough value; do not create a value named textured, which merely signals the texture attribute.
current_ontology_status: The sole occurrence is rough-textured stems.
counterexample_or_caveat: Textured alone does not state which texture value applies and is analogous to an attribute-name suffix rather than a phenotype value.

definition: A small, slender, distal branch representing recent shoot growth.
other_axioms: Promote the current NARROW synonym twig on PO branch only after a dendrological definition establishes size, developmental age, and distal-position boundaries; add twigs as the exact plural.
current_ontology_status: PO:0025073 branch carries twig as a NARROW synonym but lacks a defined subclass; the Saudi occurrence describes young flowering twigs.
counterexample_or_caveat: Small branch, branchlet, current-year shoot, and twig can overlap without being universally equivalent, so the provisional differentia needs authoritative support.

other_axioms: Normalize a bearer with many fine feather-like branches or filaments to PATO:0005010; retire the duplicate temporary FLOPO:0980122 only after reviewing every class that references it.
current_ontology_status: Current PATO defines plumose operationally and already carries feathery as an exact synonym; the released FLOPO temporary value duplicates that target.
counterexample_or_caveat: Feathery can also describe texture or motion outside branching morphology, so the bearer and fine-branch criterion remain required.

other_axioms: Apply triangular to the cross-section reference region and preserve rounded-angle trigonous versus sharp-ridged triquetrous detail when stated; replace the erroneous FLOPO:0980163 parent PATO:0000617 bent.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001875 already defines having three angles; the glossaries define trigonous and triquetrous as triangular cross sections with different angle profiles.
counterexample_or_caveat: The whole three-dimensional organ is not itself a triangle, and a triquetrous organ additionally has three longitudinal ridges; those assertions require the section and angle context.

definition: A pilosity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer having tufts of long, soft hairs that tend to rub off as small wool-like masses.
other_axioms: Add flocculose as a narrow diminutive and cottony as a related botanical synonym; migrate FLOPO:0980342 only when the corpus bearer satisfies the tufted, soft-hair and rub-off criteria.
current_ontology_status: Pinned glossaries independently define floccose; released FLOPO:0980342 cottony has only a label-paraphrase definition under generic texture.
counterexample_or_caveat: Cottony can describe colour, bulk texture, or a mass of hairs without establishing that the hairs rub off, so it is not proposed as an unrestricted exact synonym.

definition: A source-language colour phenotype preserving a compound or modified colour expression whose operational colour-space region is not supplied by the flora text.
other_axioms: Keep these expressions in FLOPO, link them to component colour candidates with an explicit mixture or modification relation rather than conjunctive is_a parents, and do not assert an operational colour value until a physical prototype or range is cited.
current_ontology_status: Released FLOPO:0980131, FLOPO:0980205, and FLOPO:0980366 exist but their definitions only paraphrase labels and list component colours.
counterexample_or_caveat: Rose-pink is not logically every red and every pink instance, pale is a degree modifier, and purple-magenta needs a mixture/continuum model; the current component restrictions must not be read as conjunctive colour subsumption.

other_axioms: Use portion of secretory tissue for a verified tissue gland, nectary for Euphorbia cyathium nectar glands when applicable, and glandular trichome only for secretory epidermal outgrowths.
current_ontology_status: Saudi uses include cyathium glands and wart-like glands; PO deliberately keeps gland only RELATED to portion of secretory tissue.
counterexample_or_caveat: A visible gland may be a tissue, cavity, trichome, or organ region, and secretion cannot be inferred solely from a wart-like appearance.

other_axioms: Normalize the male reproductive structure to PO:0030119 when it has the monopodial, sessile-unisexual-flower and bract criteria in the PO definition.
current_ontology_status: Current PO already has catkin as an exact synonym of catkin inflorescence.
counterexample_or_caveat: The vernacular word can be applied loosely to catkin-like spikes; extraction should retain sex and structural context rather than rely only on the plural.

definition: A fruit-shape phenotype in which the bearer resembles a curved, tapered animal claw without thereby being identified as a claw structure.
other_axioms: Retain the prototype comparison and measured curvature/taper when available; do not mint a PO claw entity or equate it automatically with PATO falciform.
current_ontology_status: The sole Saudi occurrence is a claw-shaped fruit with short outer-edge spines.
counterexample_or_caveat: Claws vary in curvature and cross-section, and the source gives no quantitative boundary separating claw-shaped from hooked, falcate, or tapered.

other_axioms: Normalize the flower arrangement to PO:0030124 when the axes and convex flower plane meet its definition.
current_ontology_status: Current PO already has corymb as an exact synonym of corymb inflorescence.
counterexample_or_caveat: Flat-topped or convex clusters that lack the specified growth habits and axes are not automatically corymbs.

definition: A temporal colour phenotype in which a specified bearer changes from a stated initial colour toward a stated later colour over time.
other_axioms: Bind the bearer, initial colour, later colour, and temporal relation; do not model fading as a static low-saturation value when the endpoint is explicitly white.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrence says pale blue-lilac flowers fade to white.
counterexample_or_caveat: Fading can reduce chroma, change lightness, or change hue, so it has no single PATO colour endpoint without the source context.

definition: A phenotype in which a specified marking or plant structure is aligned parallel to the principal long axis of its bearer.
other_axioms: Bind the bearer axis and the pale-green lines; retain the line colour pattern separately from its orientation.
current_ontology_status: The Saudi occurrence modifies colour lines along a corolla.
counterexample_or_caveat: Longitudinal is a relation to an axis, not a line, colour, or bearer-independent object quality by itself.

other_axioms: Represent the fruit as not in contact with or connected to the other fruits, supplying the second relational argument.
current_ontology_status: PATO:0001505 matches the structural separated sense in the Saudi description.
counterexample_or_caveat: Separated can also describe taxonomic, spatial-distance, or post-detachment states, and the target relation is incomplete without the entity separated from.
